scenario: 面试官让你为 Uber 开场定义功能需求和非功能需求，用统一句式列出来方便对齐范围。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to open the Uber design by framing functional and non-functional requirements with consistent wording so scope is easy to align.
q: 功能需求和非功能需求分别该用什么句式来写？
q_en: What sentence pattern should you use for functional vs non-functional requirements?
options: 功能需求写「系统应该...」，非功能需求写「用户应该能...」
功能需求写「用户应该能...」，非功能需求写「系统应该...」
两类需求都统一写成用户故事，不做区分
两类需求都统一写成系统质量指标，不做区分
why: 功能需求描述用户能做什么，用「用户应该能…」；非功能需求描述系统质量，用「系统应该…」。开场按这两个句式分别列出再挑核心。
why_en: Functional requirements read as user-should-be-able-to statements, while non-functional requirements read as the-system-should statements about system qualities.
options_en: Functional requirements use 'The system should...' and non-functional requirements use 'Users should be able to...'.
Functional requirements use 'Users should be able to...' and non-functional requirements use 'The system should...'.
Write both requirement types as user stories with no distinction.
Write both requirement types as system quality metrics with no distinction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统必须提供的具体用户能力，例如「乘客能请求乘车」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A functional requirement is a concrete capability the system must give users, such as letting a rider request a ride.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统必须满足的质量属性，例如延迟、一致性、吞吐量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-functional requirement is a quality attribute the system must meet, such as latency, consistency, or throughput.

optionExplanations: 这把两类需求的句式说反了：系统质量用「系统应该」描述才对，不是用户动作那句。
对，用户能做的事归「用户应该能」，系统要达到的质量归「系统应该」，两条线分得清楚。
用户故事天然讲用户动作，套不上延迟、吞吐这类系统质量约束。
质量指标的写法描述不出「乘客能做什么」这种功能行为，两类需求会混在一起。
optionExplanations_en: This swaps the two patterns — system qualities belong in a "the system should" sentence, not the user-action one.
Right: what users can do goes under "users should be able to," what the system must deliver goes under "the system should."
User stories naturally describe user actions, not quality attributes like latency or throughput.
Quality-metric wording can't express "what a rider can do," so the two requirement types blur together.

scenario: Uber 面试要求先挑出最多 3-4 条核心功能需求，其余标为 below the line。
scenario_en: In the Uber interview, pick at most three or four core functional requirements and mark the rest below the line.
q: 以下哪些属于 Uber 的核心（above the line）功能需求？
q_en: Which are Uber's core above-the-line functional requirements?
options: 乘客输入起终点，获得费用预估
乘客基于预估费用发起乘车请求
系统把请求匹配给附近可用司机，司机能接受/拒绝并导航
行程结束后乘客和司机互相评分
why: 核心三条：估价、按估价请求乘车、匹配并由司机接受导航；互评/预约/车型属于 below the line。划线是**时间盒**：面试只有 30-45 分钟设计不完全部，挑 3-4 条核心放 above the line 重点设计、其余认领但不展开——既显示你会抓重点（资深信号），又不在次要功能上耗时间。
why_en: The three core requirements are fare estimate, requesting a ride, and matching with a driver who accepts and navigates; rating/scheduling/car-tiers are below the line. Drawing the line is time-boxing: a 30-45 min interview can't design everything, so you design only the 3-4 core (above the line) and explicitly park the rest — signaling you can prioritize.
options_en: The rider enters a start and end location and gets a fare estimate.
The rider requests a ride based on the estimated fare.
The system matches the request to a nearby available driver, who can accept or decline and navigate.
After the trip, the rider and driver rate each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 划在线上、这次要重点设计的 3-4 条核心功能需求（面试时间有限，只做这些）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Above the line: the 3-4 core functional requirements you will actually design in the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 划在线下、认领但这次不展开设计的次要需求（显示你会抓重点、不耗时间在次要项）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Below the line: secondary requirements you acknowledge but deliberately do not design, to stay focused.

optionExplanations: 对，估价是整条流程的起点，没有它后面无法定价请求。
对，乘客确认价格后发起请求，这一步把估价和真正下单串起来。
对，匹配加司机接受导航是把请求变成真实行程的核心动作。
互评发生在行程结束后，不影响能否叫到车，划进 below the line 才对。
optionExplanations_en: Right, the fare estimate is where the whole flow starts — nothing downstream can price a request without it.
Right, this is the step where the rider commits the estimate into an actual request.
Right, matching plus driver accept-and-navigate is what turns a request into a real trip.
Rating happens after the ride ends and doesn't affect whether a ride happens, so it belongs below the line.

scenario: 45 分钟的 Uber 面试里，候选人只挑了 3 条功能需求作为核心，其余明确标成 below the line。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute Uber interview, the candidate picks three functional requirements as core and explicitly marks the rest below the line.
q: 只选 3 条核心需求、其余标 below the line，目的是什么？
q_en: Why pick only three core requirements and put the rest below the line?
options: 面试规则强制要求最多写 3 条
below the line 的功能今后绝口不再提
保持聚焦、能在限时内执行完整设计，同时给面试官调整优先级的机会
让需求列表显得更少更简单，方便记忆
why: 只选 top 3 是为了聚焦和限时执行；其余标 below the line 展示产品思维，并邀请面试官调整优先级。
why_en: Picking only the top requirements keeps you focused enough to execute in the limited time while below-the-line items invite reprioritization.
options_en: Interview rules cap the list at exactly three items.
Below-the-line items can never be mentioned again during the interview.
It keeps you focused and able to execute within the time limit, while giving the interviewer a chance to reprioritize.
It makes the requirement list look shorter and easier to memorize.
tradeoff: 覆盖面广 vs 有限时间内能执行完的深度
optionExplanations: 面试没有硬性数量规则，划线是候选人自己做的产品判断，不是被规定的。
被划到这轮先不展开的清单里，不代表以后不会做，面试官随时能把它调回来。
对，划线既保证 45 分钟内能做完整设计，又给面试官挪动优先级的空间。
划线的目的是执行深度而不是表面简洁，写少了但没深挖也拿不到分。
optionExplanations_en: There's no hard rule capping the count — drawing the line is the candidate's own product judgment, not an imposed rule.
Being deferred for this round doesn't mean it's dead — the interviewer can pull it back in anytime.
Right, drawing the line keeps the design achievable in 45 minutes while leaving room for the interviewer to reorder priorities.
The point is depth of execution, not looking short — fewer items without real depth still won't score well.

scenario: Uber 面试定义非功能需求时给出两个量级前提：匹配时限和峰值同地点请求量。
scenario_en: When defining Uber's non-functional requirements, the interview gives two scale assumptions: match deadline and peak same-location request volume.
q: 补全 Uber 的两个关键非功能指标：
q_en: Fill in the two key Uber non-functional targets:
text: 低延迟匹配：{{1}} 分钟内完成匹配或明确失败；高吞吐：高峰或特殊活动时，同一地点可能涌入 {{100k}} 级别的请求。
why: 这两个数字驱动后续深挖：<1 分钟要求匹配流程快且有超时兜底，同一地点 10 万级请求要求用队列削峰和地理分片来吸收。
why_en: The system must match or fail within one minute and absorb on the order of one hundred thousand requests from a single location at peak.

scenario: Uber 把「匹配强一致性」列为核心非功能需求之一。
scenario_en: Uber lists strong matching consistency as one core non-functional requirement.
q: Uber 里「匹配强一致性」具体指什么？
q_en: What does strong matching consistency mean in Uber?
options: 所有数据库副本任何时刻都字节级一致
乘客端和司机端地图渲染完全一致
费用预估金额与最终收费金额必须相同
同一司机在任意时刻只有一个待处理的乘车请求
why: 这里的强一致专指匹配：任一时刻一个司机只能有一个待处理请求，防止重复指派，直接催生后面的锁深挖。
why_en: Strong consistency here means no driver is ever assigned more than one pending ride request at the same time.
options_en: All database replicas are byte-for-byte identical at every instant.
The rider and driver apps render the exact same map.
The fare estimate must equal the final charged amount.
A driver has at most one pending ride request at any given moment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统保证所有读操作都能看到最新写入结果，不允许旧值或冲突值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency guarantees every read sees the latest write, with no stale or conflicting values.

optionExplanations: 字节级副本一致是数据库复制层面的强一致，跟这里指的匹配一致性是两回事。
地图渲染是否一致是客户端展示问题，跟司机会不会被重复指派完全无关。
预估价和实付价本来就允许有差异，这不是这里说的一致性要求。
对，这里的强一致专指同一司机任一时刻只有一个待处理请求，防止被重复指派。
optionExplanations_en: Byte-identical replicas is database-replication-level strong consistency, a different thing from the matching consistency meant here.
Whether the map renders identically is a client display concern, unrelated to whether a driver gets double-dispatched.
The fare estimate and the final charge are allowed to differ — that's not the consistency requirement referred to here.
Right, strong consistency here specifically means one driver has at most one pending request at any moment, preventing double-dispatch.

scenario: Uber 面试把非功能需求分成核心三条和 below the line 若干条。
scenario_en: The Uber interview separates non-functional requirements into three core items and several below-the-line items.
q: 以下哪些属于 Uber 题的核心非功能需求？
q_en: Which are core non-functional requirements for the Uber design?
options: 低延迟匹配：1 分钟内匹配或明确失败
符合 GDPR 的安全与隐私合规
匹配强一致：司机不会被同时指派多个请求
高吞吐：扛住高峰期同一地点的海量请求
why: 核心 NFR 三条：低延迟匹配、匹配强一致、高峰高吞吐。GDPR 合规、容灾冗余、监控告警都列为 below the line。
why_en: The core non-functional requirements are low-latency matching, strongly consistent matching, and high peak throughput.
options_en: Low-latency matching: match or fail within one minute.
Security and privacy compliance with regulations like GDPR.
Strongly consistent matching so a driver never gets two requests at once.
High throughput to absorb a surge of requests at one location.

termDefinitions.meaning: 欧盟的数据保护法规，规范用户数据的收集与处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GDPR is the EU regulation governing how user data is collected and processed.

optionExplanations: 对，1 分钟匹配时限直接决定后面要不要队列削峰和超时兜底。
GDPR 合规属于法规范畴，不改变匹配路径的架构决策，这次先不展开。
对，同一司机同时只有一个待处理请求，这条一致性要求后面直接催生锁的设计。
对，峰值同地点海量请求逼着系统必须扛得住突发写入和查询压力。
optionExplanations_en: Right, the one-minute matching deadline directly drives whether you need a queue to absorb bursts and a timeout fallback.
GDPR compliance is a legal requirement that doesn't change the matching architecture, so it's set aside for this round.
Right, one driver can only have one pending request at a time — this consistency rule is what later drives the locking design.
Right, peak same-location traffic forces the system to survive bursty writes and queries.

scenario: Uber 属于面向终端用户的产品型系统设计题，需要在满足功能需求后再深挖非功能需求。
scenario_en: Uber is a user-facing product system design problem: satisfy functional requirements first, then deep-dive into non-functional requirements.
q: 产品型系统设计题推荐的整体推进策略是什么？
q_en: What overall approach is recommended for a product-style system design problem?
options: 先把全部非功能需求解决，再回头补功能
开场直接画出最终架构图，再逐步验证
顺着功能需求逐条搭建设计，满足后再用非功能需求驱动深挖
先把数据库 schema 定下来，再回头讨论功能和非功能需求
why: 顺着功能需求一条条搭，保证不跑偏、不迷失细节；功能满足后，用非功能需求（延迟、一致性、吞吐）指引深挖方向。
why_en: Build the design sequentially through the functional requirements, then let the non-functional requirements guide the deep dives.
options_en: Resolve every non-functional requirement first, then patch in functionality afterward.
Draw the final architecture diagram immediately and validate it step by step.
Build up the design sequentially through the functional requirements, then use non-functional requirements to guide deep dives.
Lock down the database schema first, then circle back to discuss both functional and non-functional requirements.
optionExplanations: 先做非功能会让你在没有基本骨架时就纠结细节，容易在时限内走不完整个流程。
开场就画终态架构会跳过推导过程，面试官看不到你怎么一步步得出这个设计。
对，先按功能需求把骨架搭起来，再用延迟、一致性这些约束逐步深挖细节。
先定 schema 会在还没理清整体流程时就陷入字段细节，容易走偏。
optionExplanations_en: Tackling non-functional needs first leaves you arguing over details before there's a basic skeleton, and you may not finish in time.
Drawing the final architecture upfront skips the reasoning trail — the interviewer can't see how you got there.
Right, build the skeleton along functional requirements first, then let latency, consistency, and throughput drive the deep dives.
Locking the schema first pulls you into field-level detail before the overall flow is even clear.

scenario: Uber 设计需要定义支撑核心功能需求的实体，Rider 和 Driver 已经确定。
scenario_en: The Uber design needs entities for the core requirements, with Rider and Driver already decided.
q: 除了 Rider 和 Driver，还需要哪些核心实体？
q_en: Besides Rider and Driver, which core entities do you need?
options: Fare：一次乘车的预估价与预计到达时间
Payment：完整的支付流水记录
Ride：从确认请求到完成的一次行程
Location：司机的实时位置坐标
why: 五个核心实体：Rider、Driver、Fare、Ride、Location。Location 单列——高频更新、要按地理就近查询，访问模式和规模跟 driver 档案完全不同；Payment 不列——支付通常交给第三方，金额已由 Fare 承载。
why_en: Location is a separate entity because it updates every few seconds and is queried by proximity, so it needs a geo index, not a driver field. Payment is out of scope: below the line, delegated to a third party, with the amount already on Fare.
options_en: Fare: the estimated price and ETA for one ride.
Payment: the full transaction ledger.
Ride: one trip from confirmed request through completion.
Location: a driver's real-time coordinates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计到达时间，费用预估的一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ETA is the estimated time of arrival included with a fare estimate.

optionExplanations: 对，Fare 独立成实体是为了下单前就能单独算出报价，不用先建整条 Ride。
支付通常交给 Stripe 这类第三方处理，金额已经在 Fare 里，本题不需要单独建 Payment 实体。
对，Ride 记录一次行程从确认到完成的完整状态机，是串起整个流程的主实体。
对，Location 更新频率是秒级的，还要做地理临近检索，跟司机档案的读写方式完全不是一回事，因此单独放地理索引。
optionExplanations_en: Right, Fare is its own entity so a price can be computed before a full Ride record even exists.
Payments are typically handed off to a third party like Stripe, and the amount already lives on Fare, so this problem skips a Payment entity.
Right, Ride carries the full state machine of a trip from confirmation to completion — it's the entity that ties the flow together.
Right, Location refreshes on a seconds-level cadence and needs geo-proximity lookups, a totally different access pattern from a driver profile, so it gets its own geo index.

scenario: Uber 用一个独立的 Fare 实体保存费用预估，而不是直接塞进 Ride。
scenario_en: Uber keeps fare estimation in a separate Fare entity instead of putting it directly into Ride.
q: Fare 实体里应该存哪些字段？
q_en: What fields should the Fare entity store?
options: 司机的车辆品牌与型号信息
接送两地坐标、预估费用、预计到达时间
实际收费金额与行程时间戳
乘客绑定的支付方式列表
why: Fare（车费）就是「这趟收多少钱」的报价。它存：起点+终点坐标、预估价、ETA。单拎成实体是为了下单前就能独立算出报价、不必先建整个 Ride；并进 Ride 也行，说清取舍即可。
why_en: A fare is the price quote for a trip — pickup and destination coordinates, the estimated price, and the ETA. It's split out so the quote can be produced before a ride exists; it could equally live on the ride.
options_en: The driver's vehicle make and model.
The pickup and destination coordinates, the estimated fare, and the ETA.
The actual charged amount and trip timestamps.
The list of payment methods the rider has on file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 车费：一趟行程要收多少钱的报价（起点终点、预估价、ETA）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fare is the price quote for a trip: pickup/destination, estimated price, and ETA.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计到达时间
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ETA is the estimated time of arrival.

optionExplanations: 车辆品牌型号属于 Driver 或车辆档案信息，跟一次报价无关。
对，起终点坐标、预估价、ETA 是算清一次报价需要的全部输入和输出。
实际收费和时间戳属于行程结束后的结算数据，应该记在 Ride 里，不是报价阶段的 Fare。
支付方式是乘客账户信息，属于 Rider 或支付服务，不是某一次报价的属性。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle brand and model belong to the driver or vehicle profile, not to a single fare quote.
Right, pickup/dropoff coordinates, the estimated price, and the ETA are exactly what's needed to produce and use a quote.
The actual charge and timestamps are post-trip settlement data that belongs on Ride, not on a pre-trip Fare quote.
Payment methods are account-level rider data, not a property of any single fare quote.

scenario: Ride 实体要覆盖一次行程从确认到结束的完整生命周期。
scenario_en: The Ride entity should cover the full trip lifecycle from confirmation through completion.
q: Ride 实体覆盖的生命周期是哪一段？
q_en: What part of the lifecycle does the Ride entity cover?
options: 从乘客确认费用、发起请求，一直到行程完成
只覆盖乘客上车到下车这一段
从司机上线到下线的整段工作时间
从打开 App 到关闭 App 的整段会话
why: Ride 从确认 fare、发起请求开始，到行程完成为止，记录乘客/司机身份、车辆、状态、路线、最终费用和接送时间戳。
why_en: A ride spans from the moment the rider confirms the fare and requests a ride until completion.
options_en: From the moment the rider confirms the fare and requests a ride, until the trip completes.
Only the segment from pickup to drop-off.
The driver's entire online-to-offline working session.
The entire app session from open to close.
optionExplanations: 对，从乘客确认价格发起请求，一路到行程结束，中间所有状态转换都归 Ride 管。
只算上下车这一段会漏掉「已请求、已匹配、司机赶来」这几个前置状态。
司机整段在线时长会跨越多次行程，不能塞进单次 Ride 记录里。
App 会话跟一次具体行程无关，乘客可能开着 App 却没有正在进行的 Ride。
optionExplanations_en: Right, Ride spans from the rider confirming the fare through request all the way to trip completion, covering every state in between.
Limiting it to pickup-through-dropoff misses the earlier requested, matched, and en-route states.
A driver's whole online session can span many trips, so it can't be squeezed into one Ride record.
An app session is unrelated to a specific trip — a rider can have the app open with no active Ride at all.

scenario: Location 实体要支撑「就近匹配」和「行程跟踪」两个能力。
scenario_en: The Location entity supports two capabilities: nearby matching and trip tracking.
q: Location 实体存什么、用来做什么？
q_en: What does the Location entity store and what is it used for?
options: 乘客的家庭和公司常用地址
城市级别的地理围栏多边形配置数据，跟司机个体位置无关
行程结束后的完整轨迹回放数据
司机实时经纬度和最后更新时间戳，用于就近匹配与行程跟踪
why: Location 存司机实时 lat/long 和最后更新时间，是把乘客匹配给附近司机、跟踪行程进度的关键数据。
why_en: The location entity stores each driver's latest coordinates and update timestamp, powering nearby matching and ride tracking.
options_en: The rider's saved home and work addresses.
City-level geofence polygon configuration data, unrelated to any individual driver's position.
A full trip trajectory replay after the ride ends.
The driver's live latitude, longitude, and last-update timestamp, used for nearby matching and ride tracking.
optionExplanations: 常用地址是乘客画像信息，跟司机的实时坐标没关系。
城市级地理围栏是运营配置数据，不是司机个体的实时位置。
完整轨迹回放是行程结束后的历史数据，实时匹配不需要存整条轨迹。
对，实时经纬度加最后更新时间戳，既能就近匹配又能跟踪行程进度，两件事都靠它。
optionExplanations_en: Saved home/work addresses are rider profile data, unrelated to a driver's live coordinates.
City-level geofence polygons are operational config, not an individual driver's live position.
Full trajectory replay is post-trip history — live matching doesn't need the whole path stored.
Right, live lat/long plus a last-update timestamp is exactly what both proximity matching and trip tracking need.

scenario: 获取费用预估的接口设计成 POST /fare 而不是 GET /fare。

因为 POST 请求天然比 GET 更安全
因为该请求会在数据库里创建一个新的 Fare 实体
因为 GET 请求无法返回 JSON 格式的响应体
why: 语义上这是「创建资源」：服务端算价并落一条 Fare 记录，随后请求乘车时用 fareId 引用它，所以用 POST。

options_en: GET requests cannot carry latitude and longitude parameters.
POST requests are inherently more secure than GET requests.
The call creates a new fare entity in the database.
GET requests cannot return a JSON response body.

termDefinitions.meaning: 创建新资源的 HTTP 方法。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只读取、不改变服务端状态的 HTTP 方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GET is the HTTP method that only reads data without changing server state.

optionExplanations: GET 完全可以通过 query string 带经纬度参数，这不是问题所在。
POST 本身不比 GET 更安全，安全性靠鉴权和传输层加密，不是方法本身。
对，这次调用会在数据库里新建一条 Fare 记录，语义上是创建资源，该用 POST。
GET 请求同样能返回 JSON 响应体，这跟返回格式无关。
optionExplanations_en: GET can perfectly well carry lat/long as query params — that's not the actual reason.
POST isn't inherently safer than GET; safety comes from auth and transport encryption, not the verb.
Right, this call creates a new Fare record in the database — semantically that's a resource creation, which is what POST is for.
GET can return a JSON body just fine, so response format isn't the issue.

scenario: Uber 的四个核心端点串起从估价到司机接单的主流程。
scenario_en: Uber's four core endpoints connect the main flow from fare estimation to driver acceptance.
q: 补全四个核心 API 端点：
q_en: Fill in the four core API endpoints:
text: {{POST}} /fare 创建费用预估；POST /rides 发起乘车请求，body 只带 {{fareId}}；POST /drivers/location 由司机端周期性上报{{位置}}；{{PATCH}} /rides/:rideId 用于司机接受或拒绝请求。
why: 四个端点串起主流程：估价 → 请求 → 司机位置上报 → 接受/拒绝。匹配发生在后端内部，不需要显式端点。

diagram:
graph TD
    Fare[POST /fare]
    Ride[POST /rides]
    Accept[PATCH /rides/:id]
    Loc[POST /drivers/location]
    Fare --> Ride
    Ride --> Accept
    Loc --> Match[Matching]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对已有资源做局部更新的 HTTP 方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PATCH is the HTTP method used to partially update an existing resource.

scenario: 司机端周期性调用 POST /drivers/location 上报位置。
scenario_en: The driver app periodically calls POST /drivers/location to report its position.
q: 这个请求里，driverId 应该从哪里获取？
q_en: Where should driverId come from in this request?
options: 客户端把 driverId 当作普通字段写进请求 body 一起提交
服务端可信的会话 cookie 或 JWT，绝不放在 body 或路径参数里
把 driverId 拼接进 URL 的查询字符串一起发送
客户端本地缓存一份明文 driverId，每次直接读取使用
why: 身份信息必须来自服务端可信的会话或 JWT；放在 body 或 path 里客户端可随意伪造，是面试中的红旗。
why_en: The driver's identity must come from the session cookie or JWT, never from the request body or path where it could be spoofed.
options_en: The client writes driverId as a plain field into the request body.
A server-trusted session cookie or JWT, never the body or path parameters.
driverId is appended into the URL query string on every call.
The client caches a plaintext driverId locally and reads it each time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、客户端携带的身份令牌，包含可验证的用户身份信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed identity token issued by the server and carried by the client to prove who the caller is.

optionExplanations: 放进 body 让客户端能随便改成别的司机 ID，冒充别人上报位置。
对，会话或 JWT 是服务端签发和校验的凭证，客户端改不了里面的身份信息。
拼进 URL 查询字符串跟放 body 一样，照样能被客户端随意篡改。
本地明文缓存同样是客户端可控数据，一样能被伪造或篡改。
optionExplanations_en: Putting it in the body lets the client swap in any driver id and impersonate someone else's reports.
Right, a session or JWT is issued and verified server-side, so the client can't tamper with the identity inside it.
Stuffing it into the query string is just as client-controlled and forgeable as putting it in the body.
A locally cached plaintext id is still client-controlled data and can be forged the same way.

scenario: 候选人设计请求乘车接口时，让客户端在 body 里直接传 userId、时间戳和 fareEstimate。
scenario_en: In the ride-request API, the candidate lets the client send userId, timestamp, and fareEstimate directly in the body.
q: 这种设计为什么会被判定为安全红旗？
q_en: Why is this design considered a security red flag?
options: 客户端数据可被篡改：身份该取自会话/JWT，时间戳该由服务端生成，费用该从数据库读取
这些字段过长，会明显拖慢每次请求的网络传输速度
JSON 格式原生不擅长精确表示超大整数和金额小数位，容易在传输和解析中丢失精度，需要额外处理
客户端生成的时间戳容易受设备时区设置影响出错
why: 任何客户端送来的数据都不可信：用户可以改价格、伪造身份、篡改时间。这三项都必须由服务端权威来源生成或校验。
why_en: Client-supplied data cannot be trusted, so identity comes from the session, timestamps are generated server-side, and the fare is read from the database.
options_en: Client-supplied data can be tampered with: identity should come from session/JWT, timestamps from the server, and fare from the database.
These fields are long enough to noticeably slow down every request's network transfer.
JSON isn't naturally precise at representing very large integers and fractional currency amounts, easily losing precision in transit and parsing, so it needs extra handling.
Client-generated timestamps are easily thrown off by the device's timezone setting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统里可信数据和不可信数据的分界线，客户端提交的数据默认不可信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trust boundary marks where trusted data ends and untrusted client input begins.

optionExplanations: 对，身份该来自会话、时间戳该服务端生成、费用该查库——三项都交给客户端等于让人随意改价改身份。
字段长度对网络传输的影响微乎其微，这不是这里的安全隐患。
JSON 处理大整数和小数精度确实有讲究，但这不是这道红旗的原因。
时区顶多让时间戳出现小误差，不是这里真正的安全风险点。
optionExplanations_en: Right, identity should come from the session, timestamp from the server, and fare from the database — handing all three to the client lets anyone rewrite the price or identity.
Field length has negligible effect on network transfer time; that's not the security issue here.
JSON does have real precision quirks with big integers and decimals, but that's not what makes this a red flag.
Timezone settings might cause small timestamp drift at worst — that's not the actual security risk here.

scenario: 乘客确认价格后调用 POST /rides 发起乘车请求。
scenario_en: After accepting the fare, the rider calls POST /rides to request a ride.
q: POST /rides 的请求体里只需要传什么？
q_en: What should the POST /rides body contain?
options: 起点和终点的经纬度坐标
预估价格和预计到达时间
乘客自己的 userId
已被接受的那条 fareId
why: 起终点和价格都已在 Fare 实体里，乘客身份来自会话，所以 body 只要 fareId，服务端据此创建 Ride 并触发匹配。
why_en: The request body only needs the fare id, since locations and price already live on the fare and identity comes from the session.
options_en: The pickup and destination coordinates.
The estimated price and ETA.
The rider's own user id.
The id of the fare that was already accepted.
optionExplanations: 起终点坐标已经存在对应的 Fare 记录里，不需要在这一步重复传。
价格和 ETA 同样已经算好存进 Fare，重复传等于让客户端替服务端确认价格。
乘客身份该从会话里取，不该由客户端在 body 里自己声明。
对，body 只需要那条已被接受的 fareId，服务端据此建 Ride 并触发匹配，其余信息都能从 Fare 反查。
optionExplanations_en: Pickup/dropoff coordinates already live on the matching Fare record — no need to resend them here.
Price and ETA are already computed and stored on Fare; resending them would let the client dictate the price.
Rider identity should come from the session, not be declared by the client in the request body.
Right, the body just needs the accepted fareId — the server creates the Ride and kicks off matching, looking everything else up from Fare.

scenario: 司机点击接受请求后调用 PATCH /rides/:rideId，接口返回完整的 Ride 对象。
scenario_en: After a driver taps accept, the app calls PATCH /rides/:rideId and receives the full Ride object.
q: 为什么响应体要把整个 Ride 对象返回给司机端？

options: 为了让司机核对乘客绑定的支付方式
纯粹是为了方便客户端做本地缓存
里面带接驾点和目的地坐标，司机客户端据此展示并导航
这是 REST 规范强制要求接口必须返回完整全量对象
why: 接受后系统更新状态并把接驾坐标随 Ride 返回，司机端用设备 GPS 导航到接驾点。
why_en: The returned ride contains the pickup and destination coordinates so the driver's app can display them and navigate.
options_en: So the driver can verify the rider's payment method.
Purely to make client-side caching easier.
It carries the pickup and destination coordinates so the driver app can display and navigate to them.
REST conventions supposedly mandate that every endpoint must return the complete full object.
optionExplanations: 支付方式跟司机导航无关，司机接单不需要核对乘客的支付信息。
返回整个对象不是为了缓存方便，是司机端马上就要用到里面的坐标数据。
对，Ride 里带着接驾点和目的地坐标，司机端拿这些坐标直接调 GPS 导航。
REST 并不强制返回全量对象，这里返回完整 Ride 是因为客户端确实需要这些字段。
optionExplanations_en: Payment method has nothing to do with driver navigation — a driver accepting a ride doesn't need to check the rider's payment info.
Returning the full object isn't about caching convenience — the driver client needs those coordinates right away.
Right, Ride carries the pickup and destination coordinates, which the driver client feeds straight into GPS navigation.
REST doesn't mandate returning the full object — it's returned here because the client genuinely needs those fields.

scenario: Uber 的所有客户端请求先经过一个统一的入口组件再路由到具体微服务。
scenario_en: All Uber client requests first enter through one gateway before being routed to specific microservices.
q: API Gateway 在 Uber 架构里的职责是什么？

作为请求入口做路由，并集中处理鉴权、限流等横切逻辑
持久化存储 Fare 与 Ride 两张表
负责给司机发送推送通知
why: 网关是客户端请求的统一入口：路由到对应微服务，并集中处理鉴权、限流这类横切逻辑。
why_en: The API gateway is the single entry point that routes requests to microservices and handles cross-cutting concerns like authentication and rate limiting.
options_en: It directly computes the fare estimate amount.
It is the entry point that routes requests and centrally handles cross-cutting concerns like auth and rate limiting.
It persists the Fare and Ride tables.
It sends push notifications to drivers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端请求的统一入口，负责路由到微服务并处理鉴权、限流等公共逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway is the single entry point that routes client requests to microservices and handles shared concerns like auth and rate limiting.

optionExplanations: 算价是 Ride Service 的职责，网关只负责转发请求，不碰业务逻辑。

scenario: Ride Service 是 Uber 高层设计里最先加入的微服务，负责估价和行程状态。
scenario_en: Ride Service is the first microservice added in the high-level Uber design, responsible for pricing and ride state.
q: Ride Service 承担哪两项职责？
q_en: What two responsibilities does Ride Service own?

只负责把这次请求按邻近排序结果派发给最近的可用司机，不处理别的事情
只负责持久化存储司机上报的实时位置坐标数据
只负责确认推送通知是否成功送达司机客户端

存司机实时位置，这归 Location 那部分服务管，跟 Ride Service 没关系。

计算起终点之间的距离和预计行程时间

It replaces the notification service for sending pushes.

存司机位置还是 Location Service 的活，第三方地图 API 不负责存位置数据。
发推送是 Notification Service 的职责，跟地图 API 完全是两码事。
对，估价需要距离和预计时长这两个输入，直接调第三方地图服务拿到，不用自研路由算法。

Storing driver location is still Location Service's job — the third-party map API doesn't store position data.
Sending push notifications is Notification Service's job, entirely separate from the map API.
Right, pricing needs distance and duration as inputs, so it calls a third-party map service instead of building a routing algorithm from scratch.

scenario: 乘客在客户端输入起终点后触发一次费用预估请求。

q: 费用预估的正确调用链是哪一条？
q_en: What is the correct call chain for fare estimation?

options_en: Client to mapping API to ride service to database, with the gateway skipping auth.

直接查历史价格拿不到这趟起终点的实时距离和时长，估不出准确报价。

sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Rider

options_en: Skip both the database validation and state-recording steps entirely, and push a notification straight to the single nearest driver, leaving no record behind.

Call the third-party mapping API again to fully recompute the price for the whole trip from scratch.

scenario: Location Service 是为了支撑「就近匹配」而新增的组件。
scenario_en: Location Service is added to support nearby matching.
q: Location Service 的职责是什么？
q_en: What is Location Service responsible for?
options: 接收并存储司机实时位置更新，向匹配服务提供最新位置数据
计算一次行程结束时的最终收费金额
给乘客发送行程状态变化的推送通知
负责管理整个 Ride 对象从请求到完成的状态机转换逻辑
why: 司机端持续上报位置，Location Service 负责接收、存储，并把最新位置喂给匹配服务做精确高效的就近匹配。
why_en: The location service ingests and stores real-time driver locations and serves the freshest data to the matching service.
options_en: It receives and stores real-time driver location updates and feeds the freshest data to the matching service.
It computes the final charged amount when a trip ends.
It sends push notifications when a ride's status changes.
Responsible for managing the Ride object's state machine transitions from request through completion.
optionExplanations: 对，它专门负责收集并保存司机端不断更新的坐标，再把这份数据供匹配服务查询使用。
算最终收费是 Ride Service 的估价职责，跟存位置数据是两件事。
发行程状态推送归通知那部分组件管，不是这个模块该管的事。
管理 Ride 状态机转换归 Ride Service，这个组件只处理位置数据。
optionExplanations_en: Right, it is specifically tasked with collecting and saving the driver's continuously updated coordinates, making that data available for the matching service to query.
Computing the final fare is Ride Service's pricing job, a separate concern from storing location data.
Sending trip-status push notifications falls to the notification piece, not this module.
Managing the Ride state machine belongs to Ride Service — this component only handles position data.

scenario: Ride Matching Service 收到一次请求后要从多名附近可用司机里选出最优的一个。
scenario_en: Ride Matching Service receives one request and must choose the best driver from several nearby available drivers.
q: 匹配司机时会综合考虑哪些因素？
q_en: What factors are combined when matching drivers?
options: 只看谁最早上线成为可用状态
只看司机的历史评分高低
邻近度、可用性、司机评分等多因素综合排序
按随机数分配以保证绝对公平
why: 匹配算法（面试里可抽象掉）按邻近度、可用性、评分等因素给候选司机排序，产出一个 ranked list 逐个尝试。
why_en: The matching service ranks available drivers by proximity, availability, rating, and other factors to pick the best candidate.
options_en: Only who came online first.
Only the driver's historical rating.
A ranked combination of proximity, availability, driver rating, and other factors.
A random assignment to guarantee absolute fairness.
optionExplanations: 只看谁最早上线会把离乘客很远的司机排在前面，接驾时间反而变长。
只看评分会忽略司机跟乘客的实际距离，匹配到的司机可能根本不在附近。
对，邻近度、可用性、评分等多因素综合排序，产出一份候选司机的排序列表。
随机分配完全丢掉了距离信息，会把很远的司机也派给近处的乘客。
optionExplanations_en: Ranking by who came online earliest can put a far-away driver first, actually lengthening pickup time.
Ranking by rating alone ignores actual distance to the rider — the matched driver might not be nearby at all.
Right, candidates get ranked by a mix of proximity, availability, and rating into an ordered list to try.
Random assignment throws away distance entirely and can dispatch a far driver to a nearby rider.

scenario: 匹配服务选出候选司机后要立刻把请求推送到司机手机上。
scenario_en: After the matching service chooses a candidate driver, it must push the request to the driver's phone immediately.
q: 通知服务用什么渠道把新订单推给司机？
q_en: What channel does Notification Service use to push a new order to the driver?
options: 短信加邮件双通道
服务端与客户端建立的 WebSocket 长连接
站内信，司机打开 App 才能看到
iOS 走 APNs、Android 走 FCM 的系统推送
why: 推派单要能叫醒一个可能在后台 / 息屏的司机 App。WebSocket 长连接在 App 切后台或手机休眠时会被系统杀掉，达不到；APNs(iOS)/FCM(Android) 是系统级推送通道，能唤醒后台 App、还省电省连接。WebSocket 只适合前台实时场景（如行程中给乘客推司机位置）。
why_en: Dispatch must wake a driver app that may be backgrounded or asleep — a WebSocket dies when the app backgrounds, so it can't. APNs (iOS) / FCM (Android) are OS-level push channels that wake the app efficiently. WebSocket only fits foreground real-time cases like live trip tracking.
options_en: Dual-channel SMS plus email.
A persistent WebSocket connection between server and client.
An in-app inbox message the driver only sees after opening the app.
System push through Apple's APNs on iOS and Firebase Cloud Messaging on Android.

termDefinitions.meaning: 苹果的系统级推送通道，向 iOS 设备送达通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: APNs is Apple's system-level push channel that delivers notifications to iOS devices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 谷歌的推送服务，向 Android 设备送达通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FCM is Google's push service that delivers notifications to Android devices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端与服务端的持久双向连接；适合前台低延迟实时通信，但 App 切后台会被系统断开
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent bidirectional client-server connection — great for foreground real-time, but the OS drops it when the app is backgrounded.

optionExplanations: 短信邮件延迟高、也没法把订单详情结构化推送到 App 内，不适合这种毫秒级派单。
手机息屏或 App 切到后台时，长连接常被操作系统直接掐断，叫不醒司机。
站内信要司机主动打开 App 才能看到，等不来主动应答的派单会白白流失。
对，iOS 用 APNs、Android 用 FCM，这类系统级推送能在 App 后台也叫醒它，还更省电。
optionExplanations_en: SMS and email are high-latency and can't push structured order details into the app — too slow for split-second dispatch.
Once the phone sleeps or the app is backgrounded, the OS often kills a persistent connection outright, so it can't wake the driver.
An in-app inbox only gets seen once the driver opens the app, so time-sensitive dispatch offers would go unanswered and lapse.
Right, iOS uses APNs and Android uses FCM — system-level push that can wake a backgrounded app while also saving battery.

scenario: 匹配服务已经生成了一份按优先级排好序的候选司机列表。
scenario_en: The matching service has already produced a priority-ordered candidate driver list.
q: 接下来系统怎么把请求派发给候选司机？
q_en: How should the system dispatch the request to candidate drivers next?
options: 先通知榜首司机，拒绝或超时后再通知列表中下一位
同时通知列表前 5 位，谁先抢到算谁的
对整座城市的在线司机做一次广播
把候选列表展示给乘客，让乘客自己挑司机
why: 一次只发给一个司机：榜首司机接受则派单成功；拒绝或超时就顺延到列表中下一位，这正是匹配一致性要求的体现。
why_en: The system notifies only the top-ranked driver and moves to the next one if they decline or time out.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    A["匹配服务生成候选司机排序列表"] --> B["通知榜首司机 APNs/FCM"]
    B --> C{"司机响应?"}
    C -- "接受" --> D["状态置 accepted 并返回接驾坐标"]
    C -- "拒绝或超时" --> E["通知列表中下一位司机"]
    E --> C
options_en: Notify only the top-ranked driver first, then move to the next one on decline or timeout.
Notify the top five simultaneously and let whoever accepts first win.
Broadcast the request to every online driver in the city.
Show the candidate list to the rider and let them pick a driver.
optionExplanations: 对，先通知排第一的司机，拒绝或超时才顺延下一位，这样任何时刻一个司机只被锁定一个请求。
同时通知前 5 位会让多个司机同时被同一个请求占用，破坏「同一时刻只有一个待处理请求」的一致性要求。
对全城广播既浪费通知资源，也一样会造成多个司机同时抢一单的竞态。
把候选列表甩给乘客选，等于把匹配算法的排序工作丢给用户，也拖慢了整个流程。
optionExplanations_en: Right, notify the top-ranked driver first; only move to the next one on a reject or timeout, keeping one pending request per driver at any moment.
Notifying the top 5 at once lets several drivers get tied up by the same request simultaneously, breaking the one-pending-request-per-driver rule.
Broadcasting citywide wastes notification capacity and still creates a race where multiple drivers grab the same request.
Handing the ranked list to the rider offloads the ranking work onto the user and slows the whole flow down.

scenario: 司机在客户端点击「接受」按钮，触发 PATCH /rides/:rideId。
scenario_en: The driver taps accept in the client, triggering PATCH /rides/:rideId.
q: 司机接受后，Ride Service 具体做哪两件事？
q_en: After a driver accepts, what two things does Ride Service do?
options: 把这次行程重新估价一遍，并立即从乘客账户里扣款
把 ride 状态更新为 accepted、写入指派司机，并把接驾坐标返回司机端
把这条已经生成好、还在使用中的 Fare 记录直接从数据库里永久删除掉
群发通知告诉其他候选司机这单订单已经被抢走了
why: 接受即落定：状态更新为 accepted、记录指派司机，然后返回接驾点坐标，司机用设备 GPS 导航前往。
why_en: On acceptance the ride status becomes accepted with the driver assigned, and the pickup coordinates are returned for navigation.
diagram:
graph LR
    Driver[Driver accepts] --> Ride[Ride Service]
    Ride --> Lock[Validate assignment lock]
    Lock --> State[Set ride accepted]
    State --> Notify[Notify rider and driver]
    State --> Persist[(Ride DB)]
options_en: Recompute the fare for this trip from scratch and immediately charge the rider's account.
Update the ride status to accepted with the assigned driver, and return the pickup coordinates.
Permanently delete the already-generated Fare record, one still in active use, straight out of the database.
Broadcast to every other candidate driver that this order has already been taken.
optionExplanations: 价格在 Fare 阶段已经定了，接受订单这一步不重新估价也不立即扣款。
对，状态改成 accepted、记下指派司机，再把接驾坐标返回给司机端导航。
Fare 记录还要留着结算和历史查询用，接受订单不会删掉它。
群发通知别的候选司机不是这一步该做的事，其他司机本来就没被通知到这单。
optionExplanations_en: The price was already locked in at the Fare stage — accepting doesn't re-price or charge the rider immediately.
Right, the status flips to accepted, the assigned driver is recorded, and pickup coordinates go back to the driver client for navigation.
The Fare record still needs to exist for settlement and history, so accepting doesn't delete it.
Broadcasting a "this order is taken" message to other candidates isn't part of this step — they were never notified in the first place.

scenario: 面试官给出量级前提：约 1000 万司机，每人每 5 秒上报一次位置，要求算出峰值写入速率来判断存储选型。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives a scale assumption: about 10 million drivers, each reporting location every 5 seconds; calculate peak write rate to choose storage.
q: 1000 万司机、每 5 秒上报一次位置，写入速率大约是多少？
q_en: With 10 million drivers reporting every 5 seconds, what is the approximate write rate?
options: 每秒约 2 万次写入
每秒约 20 万次写入
每秒约 200 万次写入
每秒约 2000 次写入
why: 10M ÷ 5s = 200 万次写/秒。这个量级直接宣判「逐条写进 Postgres/DynamoDB」不可行：要么被写垮，要么贵到离谱，逼出批处理或内存方案。
why_en: Ten million drivers pinging every five seconds is roughly two million location writes per second, which is downstream input for choosing the storage layer.
options_en: Roughly twenty thousand writes per second.
Roughly two hundred thousand writes per second.
Roughly two million writes per second.
Roughly two thousand writes per second.
optionExplanations: 把 1000 万除以 5 秒少算了两个数量级，实际应该是每秒 200 万次量级。
这个数字比正确值小了一个数量级，1000 万除以 5 秒的量级要再乘 10。
对，1000 万除以 5 秒约等于 200 万次每秒，这是压垮传统数据库、逼出批处理或内存方案的关键量级。
这个数字比正确答案小了三个数量级，明显算错了除法。
optionExplanations_en: Dividing 10 million by 5 seconds and landing here is off by two orders of magnitude from the real ~2 million per second.
This is an order of magnitude too low — 10 million divided by 5 seconds lands about 10x higher.
Right, 10 million divided by 5 seconds is about 2 million writes per second, the magnitude that rules out a naive database and forces batching or an in-memory approach.
This is off by about three orders of magnitude from the correct division.

scenario: 已知位置写入约 200 万次/秒、每条约 100 字节，评估用按需计费的 DynamoDB（约 $1.25/百万写请求单元）直接承接这批写入的日成本。
scenario_en: Location writes are about 2 million per second, each about 100 bytes; estimate on-demand DynamoDB at about $1.25 per million write request units.
q: 按此写入量和单价，DynamoDB 承接原始位置写入一天大约花多少钱？
q_en: Given this write rate and price, roughly how much would DynamoDB cost per day for raw location writes?
options: 超过 20 万美元一天
大约 2000 美元一天
大约 200 美元一天
几乎不产生费用
why: 200 万/秒持续一天是天文数字级的写请求，按 $1.25/百万算超过 20 万美元/天。这个成本锚点说明位置写入必须换存储方案，而不是直接用按需 DynamoDB。
why_en: At on-demand pricing two million writes per second costs over two hundred thousand dollars a day, which rules out DynamoDB for raw location writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按需模式下按请求量计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL key-value and document database, billed per request under on-demand mode.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 按需模式下每次写请求消耗的计费单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WRU is the billing unit DynamoDB charges for each write request under on-demand pricing.

options_en: More than two hundred thousand dollars a day.
About two thousand dollars a day.
About two hundred dollars a day.
Almost no cost at all.
optionExplanations: 对，200 万次每秒按每百万写请求单元 1.25 美元算，一天下来轻松超过 20 万美元，这个成本直接排除按需 DynamoDB。
这个数字比真实量级低了近百倍，没把 200 万次每秒按一整天累计计算。
这个数字更是低了上千倍，明显没考虑到写入是持续一整天的规模。
这个量级的写入不可能几乎不花钱，忽略计费单价直接得出这个结论是不对的。
optionExplanations_en: Right, at $1.25 per million write request units with roughly 2 million writes per second sustained all day, the bill easily clears two hundred thousand dollars, which rules out on-demand DynamoDB outright.
This is nearly a hundred times too low — it doesn't account for 2 million writes per second sustained over a full day.
This is off by roughly a thousand times, ignoring that the write volume runs continuously all day.
Write volume this large can't cost next to nothing — reaching that conclusion ignores the per-request billing rate entirely.

scenario: 初版设计把每条位置更新直接写库，就近查询时用原始 lat/long 逐行计算距离。
scenario_en: The first design writes every location update directly to the database and computes distance by scanning raw lat/long rows.
q: 这个 naive 方案在千万司机规模下会导致什么后果？
q_en: What happens to this naive design at ten-million-driver scale?
options: 只是运营成本会略微上升一点点，功能本身完全不受任何影响，用户体验也不会变差
只会对司机端手机的电量消耗产生轻微影响
偶尔出现少量数据丢失，但不影响整体匹配质量
写入压垮数据库，查询要全表扫描算距离，系统过载、延迟高、完全不可扩展
why: 这是 bad approach：百万级司机的写入洪峰加上无地理索引的全表距离计算，双重不可扩展，直接导致过载和糟糕的用户体验。
why_en: Writing every raw update and scanning the whole table for proximity both collapse at scale, causing overload and high latency.
options_en: Only a very slight uptick in operating cost, with the feature itself completely unaffected and no degradation to the user experience.
It only slightly affects the driver app's battery consumption.
Occasional minor data loss happens but overall matching quality is unaffected.
Writes overwhelm the database and queries require a full-table distance scan, causing overload, high latency, and no scalability.
optionExplanations: 这远不是成本小幅上涨的问题，写入洪峰会直接把数据库打垮。
电量消耗是客户端上报频率的问题，跟这里写入压垮数据库、查询全表扫描没关系。
问题不是偶尔丢一点数据，而是系统性的写入过载和查询超时。
对，千万级写入洪峰加上无索引的全表距离计算，双重压垮系统，延迟飙升甚至完全不可用。
optionExplanations_en: This is far worse than a minor cost bump — the write flood would take the database down outright.
Battery drain is about client-side reporting frequency, unrelated to the database write overload and full-table-scan queries here.
This isn't occasional minor data loss — it's systemic write overload and query timeouts across the board.
Right, the write flood from millions of drivers plus unindexed full-table distance scans compound into overload, soaring latency, and an unusable system.

scenario: 有人提议给 lat/long 两列直接加普通 B-tree 索引来加速就近查询。
scenario_en: Someone proposes adding a normal B-tree index on the lat/long columns to speed up nearby-driver queries.
q: 为什么 B-tree 索引不适合给经纬度做就近搜索？
q_en: Why is a B-tree index a poor fit for nearest-neighbor search on latitude and longitude?
options: 因为 B-tree 索引只支持字符串类型的列
B-tree 面向一维有序数据，经纬度是二维的，传统索引无法高效做邻近查询
因为建索引的过程会长时间锁表
因为经纬度是浮点数值，B-tree 索引完全不支持浮点数之间的比较运算
why: 传统 B-tree 面向一维有序数据；地理坐标是二维的，邻近查询需要空间索引（quad-tree、geohash 等），否则性能极差。
why_en: B-tree indexes handle one-dimensional ordered data and perform poorly on two-dimensional geographic proximity queries, which need spatial indexing.
options_en: B-tree indexes only support string-typed columns.
B-trees handle one-dimensional ordered data, but coordinates are two-dimensional, so traditional indexes can't do efficient proximity queries.
Building the index locks the table for a long time.
Because latitude and longitude are floating-point values, and B-tree indexes don't support float comparison operations at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种平衡树索引结构，擅长一维有序数据的范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced tree index structure that excels at range queries over one-dimensional ordered data.

optionExplanations: B-tree 完全能给数值列建索引，问题不在数据类型限制。
对，B-tree 只擅长一维有序范围查询，经纬度是二维数据，邻近查询套不上它。
建索引确实可能短暂锁表，但那不是它做不好邻近查询的原因。
B-tree 对浮点数比较没问题，真正的限制在维度而不在数据类型。
optionExplanations_en: B-tree indexes work fine on numeric columns — the limitation isn't the data type.
Right, B-tree is built for one-dimensional ordered range queries; lat/long is two-dimensional, which proximity search can't map onto it.
Index builds can briefly lock a table, but that's not why B-tree fails at proximity queries.
B-tree compares floats just fine — the real limitation is dimensionality, not data type.

scenario: 位置更新写入量约 200 万次/秒，直接逐条写库不可行；先考虑一个不引入新数据库、单纯降低写次数的通用手段。
scenario_en: Location updates are about 2 million writes per second, so writing each row directly is impossible; first consider a general way to reduce write count without adding a new database.
q: 哪种手段能显著减少数据库写操作次数？
q_en: What technique can significantly reduce the number of database writes?
options: 给位置表加更多列上的索引
把每一条位置更新都单独包进一个独立事务再提交
在短时间窗口内聚合位置更新，然后一次性批量写入
把主库复制方式从异步改成同步
why: 批处理不是把不同司机合成一条——是把很多条**不同**的写打成一包、一次往返/一次提交发出（每个司机还是各自的 key）。省的是每条写的固定开销（网络往返 / commit / WAL flush / 锁）：逐条 200 万次往返 → 攒批后砍几个数量级。
why_en: Batching doesn't merge different drivers — it packs many separate writes (each driver keeps its own key) into one round-trip/commit, amortizing the fixed per-write cost (round-trip, commit, WAL flush, locks). 2M individual writes become far fewer batched round-trips.
whenOtherWins: 如果匹配质量要求位置始终实时最新，批量窗口带来的陈旧不可接受，应直接上 Redis 实时地理索引。
tradeoff: 写吞吐 vs 位置新鲜度
options_en: Add more indexes on the location table's columns.
Wrap each individual position update in its own separate transaction before committing it.
Aggregate location updates over a short time window, then write them in one batch.
Switch primary replication from asynchronous to synchronous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多条更新在时间窗口内合并成一次批量写操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batching merges many updates within a time window into a single bulk write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条 GEOADD 命令就能带多个 (成员, 经纬度)，不同司机 ID 一条命令写入；再配合 pipelining 更省往返
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single GEOADD can carry many (member, lon, lat) triples — different driver IDs in one command; pipelining batches more.

optionExplanations: 加索引能加速查询，但每条写入照样要单独落盘，写次数一次没少。
给每条更新单独开事务只会增加提交开销，反而让写次数更贵，跟目标相反。
对，在窗口内把很多条不同司机的写攒成一批一次性提交，省掉的是逐条网络往返和 commit 的固定开销，代价是数据新鲜度打折。
改成同步复制影响的是主从一致性，跟减少主库收到的写请求次数无关。
optionExplanations_en: More indexes speed up reads but every update still lands as its own write — the write count doesn't drop.
Wrapping each update in its own transaction only adds commit overhead, making writes more expensive, the opposite of the goal.

scenario: 比较批量落库方案与 Redis GEOADD 方案在「位置数据新鲜度」这一个维度上的差别。
