options_en: A periodic job keeps a companion sorted set keyed by last-update time and removes drivers past a threshold (e.g. thirty seconds) from both sets.
Set one single blanket TTL over the entire geo key's whole dataset, without distinguishing at all whose driver data it actually belongs to.
Periodically and completely restart the whole Redis instance to wipe memory and start clean.
Push the entire job of identifying and filtering out ghost drivers down to the rider client to figure out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放地理成员及其地理分值的 Redis 有序集合，本质就是 sorted set。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geo set is a Redis sorted set that stores members and their geo-encoded scores.

optionExplanations: 对，用一个按最后上报时间打分的辅助有序集合，周期任务把超时成员从两处一起清掉，补上 geo set 没有按成员过期这个缺口。
给整个 key 设一个 TTL 会把所有司机的位置一起清空，活跃司机也会被误删。
定期重启整个 Redis 实例代价太大，还会把活跃司机的位置一起清没。
把幽灵司机过滤丢给客户端处理，客户端根本拿不到全量司机位置数据去判断。
optionExplanations_en: Right, a helper sorted structure keyed on last-report time lets a periodic job remove stale members from both places, filling the gap that geo sets have no per-member timeout.
Setting a TTL on the whole key would wipe every driver's position at once, including active ones.
Periodically restarting the whole Redis instance is far too heavy-handed and would also wipe active drivers' positions.
Pushing ghost-driver filtering to the client doesn't work — the client never has the full set of driver positions to judge from.

scenario: Redis 是内存存储，司机位置数据在宕机时可能丢失，需要评估合理的缓解手段。
scenario_en: Redis is in-memory storage, so driver location data can be lost during an outage; evaluate reasonable mitigations.
q: 哪些是应对 Redis 宕机丢位置数据的合理缓解措施？
q_en: Which mitigations are reasonable for Redis losing location data during an outage?
options: 开启 RDB 或 AOF 持久化，周期性把内存快照落盘
用 Redis Sentinel 做主从自动故障转移
每次写位置都同步再写一份到 Postgres
接受少量丢失：位置每 5 秒重传一次，几秒内状态即可自愈重建
why: RDB/AOF 降低丢失量、Sentinel 保高可用；更关键的洞察是位置 5 秒一刷，即使全丢也几秒就重建，影响天然有限。同步双写 Postgres 正是被否掉的高成本方案。
why_en: Enable RDB or AOF persistence and Sentinel failover, and note that five-second location pings rebuild any lost state within seconds anyway.
options_en: Enable RDB or AOF persistence to periodically flush the in-memory snapshot to disk.
Use Redis Sentinel for automatic primary failover.
Synchronously double-write every location update to Postgres too.
Accept small losses: positions repost every five seconds so state self-heals within seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 周期性把内存数据整体快照写到磁盘的持久化方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDB is a Redis persistence mode that periodically snapshots the whole in-memory dataset to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 把每条写命令追加写入日志文件的持久化方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is a Redis persistence mode that appends every write command to a log file.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的高可用组件，监控主节点并在故障时自动提升从节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel is the high-availability component that monitors the primary and automatically promotes a replica on failure.

optionExplanations: 对，RDB/AOF 周期性把内存快照落盘，挡住的是进程重启后数据全部归零的风险。
对，Sentinel 做主从自动故障转移，挡住的是单实例宕机导致整个位置存储不可用的风险。
每次写都同步双写 Postgres 会让写路径多一次同步落盘，直接把百万级写入吞吐拖垮，代价远超收益。
对，位置本身 5 秒一刷，就算全丢也只是几秒空窗，把恢复成本降到几乎可以忽略。
optionExplanations_en: Right, RDB/AOF periodically flushes the in-memory snapshot to disk, guarding against total data loss on a restart.
Right, Sentinel handles automatic primary failover, guarding against a single instance outage taking down the whole location store.
Synchronously dual-writing every update to Postgres adds a blocking disk write to the hot path, which would collapse million-per-second throughput — the cost dwarfs the benefit.
Right, since positions refresh every 5 seconds anyway, even a total loss only leaves a few-second gap, making recovery cost close to negligible.

q: 把「司机位置存储选型」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the driver location storage choice decision chain in the correct order:
steps: 缓解：RDB/AOF 持久化 + Sentinel 故障转移；位置每 5 秒重传，状态几秒内自愈
需求：约 1000 万司机、每 5 秒上报（约 200 万写/秒），还要低延迟就近查询
代价：纯内存存储，宕机或断电可能丢数据
选型：Redis 地理命令——geohash 进 sorted set，GEOADD 写入、GEOSEARCH 查询
why: 决策链：需求(~200万写/秒 + 就近查询) → 选 Redis 地理索引(内存) → 代价(纯内存易丢) → 缓解。缓解=RDB/AOF 落盘 + Sentinel 自动故障转移 + 位置每 5 秒重报(高频临时数据，丢了也几秒自愈)。
why_en: The chain: ~2M writes/s + proximity search → an in-memory Redis geo index → its durability cost → mitigate with RDB/AOF, Redis Sentinel auto-failover, and 5s re-reporting that self-heals lost location data within seconds.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求: 200万写/秒 + 近邻查询"] --> C["选型: Redis GEO"]
    C --> K["代价: 内存数据宕机可能丢"]
    K --> M["缓解: RDB/AOF + failover + 5秒自愈"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 高可用组件：监控主/从节点，主库挂了自动把一个从库提升为新主（故障转移），几秒内恢复；管的是服务器角色，不是司机位置
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel monitors master and replica nodes and automatically promotes a replica if the master fails — recovering in seconds.

scenario: 千万级司机固定每 5 秒上报位置，服务器与带宽压力巨大；想智能减少上报次数又不牺牲定位精度。
scenario_en: Ten million drivers report location every 5 seconds, creating heavy server and bandwidth pressure; the goal is to reduce reports intelligently without losing location accuracy.
q: 在这个约束下，减少位置上报量的最佳做法是？
q_en: Under this constraint, what is the best way to reduce location report volume?
options: 统一把每一位司机的上报间隔都固定拉长到 60 秒，不再随情况变化
改成司机只有在正式接单之后才开始上报位置
只针对单条位置报文本身做字节层面的压缩处理
自适应上报间隔：按速度、方向变化、附近待处理请求、司机状态动态调整频率
why: 客户端用设备传感器和算法决定最优上报间隔：静止/慢速就降频，快速移动或频繁转向就升频，既减少上报又保精度。
why_en: Adaptive intervals let the driver app adjust update frequency based on speed, heading changes, nearby requests, and status, cutting pings without losing accuracy.
whenOtherWins: 规模小或客户端算力受限时，固定 5 秒间隔实现简单、完全够用，自适应算法的设计测试成本不划算。
tradeoff: 上报量与带宽 vs 位置精度
options_en: Uniformly stretch every single driver's reporting interval to a fixed sixty seconds that never changes with conditions.
Only start posting location updates after the driver formally accepts a ride.
Only apply byte-level compression to a single location message itself.
Adapt the interval dynamically based on speed, heading changes, nearby pending requests, and driver status.
optionExplanations: 把所有司机统一拉到 60 秒一次，静止的司机省了流量，但疾驰司机的位置会明显滞后，牺牲了精度。
只有接单后才上报，会让匹配阶段完全看不到司机的实时位置，匹配质量直接受损。
压缩报文字节能省一点传输量，但上报次数本身完全没变，治标不治本。
对，按速度、方向变化、附近请求和司机状态动态调整频率，静止时降频省流量，移动快时升频保精度。
optionExplanations_en: A flat 60-second interval for everyone saves bandwidth on stationary drivers but leaves fast-moving drivers' positions stale — trading away precision.
Reporting only after acceptance leaves matching completely blind to real-time driver positions before that point, hurting match quality.
Byte-level compression shrinks each message but does nothing to the number of reports sent — it treats the symptom, not the cause.
Right, dynamically tuning frequency by speed, direction change, nearby pending requests, and driver status — lower when stationary to save bandwidth, higher when moving fast to keep precision.

scenario: 自适应上报算法需要参考多个上下文信号来决定当前该多久上报一次。
scenario_en: An adaptive reporting algorithm uses several context signals to decide how often to report location.
q: 自适应上报间隔会参考哪些上下文因素？
q_en: What context signals does adaptive reporting use?
options: 司机当前的行驶速度
司机行进方向的变化幅度
司机手机的剩余电量百分比
与待处理乘车请求的邻近度、司机当前状态
why: 参考因素：速度、方向变化、与待处理请求的邻近度、司机状态。静止降频，疾驰或频繁变向升频。
why_en: The interval adapts to speed, direction changes, proximity to pending ride requests, and driver status.
options_en: The driver's current driving speed.
How much the driver's heading is changing.
The remaining battery percentage on the driver's phone.
Proximity to pending ride requests and the driver's current status.
optionExplanations: 对，速度直接决定位置变化快慢，是调整上报频率最直接的信号。
对，方向变化剧烈意味着路径在拐弯，位置更容易偏离上一次上报点。
电量百分比是设备状态，不是位置变化速度的信号，不该拿来决定上报频率。
对，附近有待处理请求或司机状态变化时，更新位置对匹配更关键，值得升频。
optionExplanations_en: Right, speed directly determines how fast the position changes, making it the most direct signal for tuning frequency.
Right, sharp direction changes mean the driver is turning, so the position drifts further from the last report.
Battery percentage is a device state, not a signal of how fast position is changing, so it shouldn't drive reporting frequency.
Right, when a pending request is nearby or driver status changes, fresher position data matters more for matching, which justifies a higher rate.

scenario: 自适应算法要在「省流量」和「保精度」之间选一个安全的降频时机。
scenario_en: The adaptive algorithm must choose a safe moment to save bandwidth without sacrificing location accuracy.
q: 自适应上报下，什么时候可以安全地降低上报频率？
q_en: When can adaptive reporting safely lower the report frequency?
options: 司机静止或缓慢移动时
司机正在高速行驶时
司机正在频繁变向时
附近刚出现待处理请求时
why: 静止或慢速时位置几乎不变，降频不损精度；高速行驶或频繁转向时位置变化快，必须升频。
why_en: Updates can be less frequent when the driver is stationary or slow, and more frequent when moving fast or changing direction often.
options_en: When the driver is stationary or moving slowly.
When the driver is driving at high speed.
When the driver is changing direction frequently.
When a pending request just appeared nearby.
optionExplanations: 对，位置在停稳或低速时变化很小，把上报间隔拉长不会让匹配用到明显滞后的坐标。
高速行驶时位置变化很快，这时候降频反而会让匹配用上过时坐标。
频繁变向说明路径在快速改变，这正是需要升频而不是降频的场景。
附近出现待处理请求时更需要精确位置去匹配，这时候应该升频而不是降频。
optionExplanations_en: Right, position barely shifts once a driver is stopped or crawling, so stretching out the interval doesn't feed matching a noticeably stale coordinate.
At high speed the position changes fast, so lowering frequency here would feed matching a stale coordinate.
Frequent direction changes mean the path is shifting quickly — that calls for a higher rate, not a lower one.
A nearby pending request needs precise position for matching, which calls for a higher rate, not a lower one.

scenario: 自适应上报这个深挖背后藏着一条更普遍的面试设计教训。
scenario_en: The adaptive-reporting deep dive carries a more general system-design interview lesson.
q: 自适应上报这个深挖给出的更普遍的设计教训是什么？
q_en: What broader design lesson does the adaptive-reporting deep dive teach?
options: 客户端应该尽量少写业务逻辑，越薄越好
别忽视客户端：很多系统的效率靠客户端逻辑，如文件上传里客户端负责分块压缩
所有性能优化工作都应该只在服务端一侧完成
客户端只该负责渲染界面，绝不应该碰任何一点业务逻辑或计算工作
why: 很多候选人画个小小的 client 框就略过。其实客户端常承担关键优化：这里是用设备传感器决定上报间隔，文件上传场景则是客户端分块与压缩。
why_en: Do not neglect the client, since client-side logic like adaptive pings or upload chunking often drives system efficiency and scalability.
options_en: The client should carry as little business logic as possible.
Do not neglect the client: much of a system's efficiency comes from client logic, like chunking and compression in file uploads.
All performance optimization work should happen only on the server side.
The client should only render the interface and must never touch any business logic or computation at all.
optionExplanations: 这道题恰恰说明客户端不该越薄越好——自适应上报这类关键优化就得放在客户端做。
对，很多候选人画个小客户端框就跳过，其实客户端常挑大梁：这里是用传感器定上报间隔，文件上传里则是分块压缩。
只在服务端做优化会漏掉客户端能做得更好的事，比如设备本地感知到的速度和方向。
客户端只负责渲染的说法正是这道深挖要纠正的误区，它经常承担关键业务逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: This exact deep-dive shows the opposite — the client shouldn't be as thin as possible; key optimizations like adaptive reporting live there.
Right, many candidates sketch a tiny client box and move on, but clients often carry key optimizations — sensor-driven reporting here, chunking and compression for uploads elsewhere.
Doing optimization only server-side misses things the client is better positioned for, like locally sensed speed and direction.
"Client should only render" is exactly the misconception this deep-dive corrects — clients often own meaningful business logic.

scenario: 派单后需要给司机一个固定的响应窗口，超时就顺延给下一位候选司机，这个设计模式在别的题目里也出现过。
scenario_en: After dispatch, the system gives the driver a fixed response window; on timeout it tries the next candidate, a pattern seen in another classic problem.
q: 司机的响应窗口时长与哪道经典题的核心机制几乎同构？
q_en: Which classic problem shares almost the same core mechanism as the driver response window?
options: 60 秒的响应等待窗口；这个设计机制被普遍认为类似于 Yelp 的评论排序问题
30 秒窗口；类似网页爬虫的抓取节流问题
5 秒窗口；类似 URL 短链的生成问题
10 秒窗口；类似 Ticketmaster 结账时临时锁票、只能卖一次的问题
why: 司机有 10 秒响应窗口，超时就顺延给下一位。这与 Ticketmaster 的锁票问题几乎一样：资源在限定时间内被独占预留。
why_en: Drivers get ten seconds to respond, mirroring Ticketmaster's problem of temporarily reserving a ticket during checkout so it sells only once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结账窗口内把一张票临时锁定给一个用户、超时释放的经典一致性问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Ticketmaster locking problem temporarily reserves a ticket for one user during checkout and releases it on timeout.

options_en: A sixty-second response waiting window; this design mechanism is widely considered similar to Yelp's review-ranking problem.
A thirty-second window, similar to a web crawler's throttling problem.
A five-second window, similar to a URL shortener's id-generation problem.
A ten-second window, similar to Ticketmaster temporarily locking a ticket during checkout so it sells only once.
optionExplanations: 60 秒和 Yelp 评论排序都对不上——评论排序跟限时锁定资源完全是两个问题。
30 秒和爬虫节流也对不上——节流控制的是请求速率，不是给一个资源限时占用。
5 秒和短链生成同样不沾边——短链生成是个 ID 分配问题，没有「限时独占」这个机制。
对，10 秒响应窗口和 Ticketmaster 结账锁票同构：资源在限定时间内被一个人独占，超时释放给别人。
optionExplanations_en: Neither the 60-second window nor Yelp's review ranking fits — ranking reviews has nothing to do with time-boxing a resource.
Neither 30 seconds nor crawler throttling fits — throttling controls request rate, not a time-limited hold on a resource.
Neither 5 seconds nor URL-shortener id generation fits — that's an id-allocation problem, no time-boxed exclusivity involved.
Right, the 10-second window mirrors Ticketmaster's checkout lock: one party holds a resource exclusively for a fixed time, then it's released on timeout.

scenario: 第一版方案让每个 Ride Matching Service 实例在自己内存里给司机「加锁 + 定时器」。
scenario_en: The first version lets each Ride Matching Service instance keep a driver lock and timer in its own memory.
q: 这种纯应用内存加锁的方案存在哪些问题？
q_en: What problems does this pure in-memory application locking design have?
options: 多实例之间无集中协调，两个实例可能同时锁同一司机，产生竞态
实例设锁后崩溃，其他实例不知道这把锁，请求可能被无限期锁死
实例数越多协调越难，出错与不一致的概率随规模上升
加锁操作会把数据库连接池直接耗尽
why: 应用级锁三宗罪：缺乏集中协调导致竞态、崩溃后锁状态不一致（无限期锁死）、随实例数增加协调问题恶化。
why_en: Application-level locks suffer race conditions across instances, orphaned locks after crashes, and coordination that degrades as the system scales.
options_en: With no centralized coordination across instances, two instances can lock the same driver at once, causing a race.
If an instance sets a lock and crashes, other instances don't know about it, so the request can stay locked forever.
The more instances there are, the harder coordination gets, raising the odds of errors and inconsistency.
Acquiring a lock directly exhausts the database connection pool.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个执行流同时争抢同一份状态、结果依赖执行顺序的错误场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition happens when multiple execution flows contend for the same state and the outcome depends on timing.

optionExplanations: 对，各实例的内存锁互相看不见，两个实例可能同时把同一个司机锁给不同请求。
对，锁状态只活在进程内存里，实例一崩溃这把锁就没人知道，司机可能永远卡在锁定状态。
对，实例越多，各自内存状态越难对齐，竞态和不一致出现的概率跟着规模一起上升。
加锁只是内存操作，不涉及数据库连接，不会把连接池占满。
optionExplanations_en: Right, each instance's in-memory lock is invisible to the others, so two instances can lock the same driver to different requests at once.
Right, the lock only lives in process memory — once that instance crashes, no one else knows about it, and the driver can stay locked forever.
Right, more instances means more independent memory states to keep aligned, so races and inconsistency grow worse with scale.
Locking is a pure in-memory operation with no database connection involved, so it wouldn't exhaust a connection pool.

scenario: 多实例各自在内存加锁有竞态和崩溃遗锁问题，想不引入新组件、用已有数据库解决跨实例协调。
scenario_en: Multiple instances have race conditions and leaked locks with in-memory locking; solve cross-instance coordination with the existing database and no new component.
q: 不新增组件、用数据库解决派单协调，该怎么做？
q_en: How can you coordinate dispatch with the database without adding a new component?
options: 让每个服务实例各自在本地加一把互斥锁，并互相广播各自持有的锁状态
把锁移进数据库：用事务把司机状态置成 outstanding_request，再改回 accepted 或 available
给同一司机产生的所有请求都统一配置好粘性会话，固定路由到同一个服务实例上去处理，其余全部实例完全不参与任何协调工作
把系统里所有的匹配请求全部改成全局串行处理，同一时刻只允许处理一个请求
why: 数据库事务保证同一时刻只有一个实例能锁定该司机：发请求时置 outstanding_request，接受/拒绝时相应更新状态，配合超时机制释放。
why_en: Moving the lock into the database uses transactions to set the driver's status to outstanding-request so only one instance can lock a driver at a time.
whenOtherWins: 若想彻底摆脱内存超时和 cron 兜底，Redis TTL 锁到期自动释放更干净；数据库锁的优势是零新增组件。
diagram:
graph LR
    Offer[Send offer] --> Lock[DB status lock]
    Lock --> Wait{Driver response}
    Wait -->|accept| Commit[Commit ride]
    Wait -->|timeout| Release[Timer releases lock]
tradeoff: 零新增组件 vs 内存定时器带来的释放不可靠
options_en: Have each service instance add its own local mutex and broadcast its held lock state to the others.
Move the lock into the database: a transaction sets the driver status to outstanding-request, then flips it to accepted or available.
Configure sticky sessions uniformly so every request generated for the same driver always routes to one fixed service instance, with every other instance left completely out of the coordination.
Serialize every matching request in the whole system globally so only one is processed at any given moment.
codeSample:
UPDATE drivers
SET status = 'outstanding_request'
WHERE id = :driverId AND status = 'available'
// 受影响行数为 0 说明抢锁失败，换下一位候选司机
optionExplanations: 本地互斥锁加广播还是各实例各管各的内存状态，广播本身有延迟和丢失风险，没解决根本的协调问题。
对，把司机状态在数据库里置为占用中、事务保证任意时刻只会被一个实例抢到，接受或拒绝后再切回对应状态。
粘性会话只是把同一司机的请求固定路由到一个实例，实例本身崩溃时协调照样失效。
把所有匹配请求改成全局串行会直接拖垮整个系统的吞吐，代价远超收益。
optionExplanations_en: A local mutex plus broadcast still leaves each instance managing its own memory state, and the broadcast itself can be delayed or lost — it doesn't solve the underlying coordination problem.
Right, flip the driver's status to a pending flag inside a database transaction, whose atomicity guarantees only one instance grabs it at a time, then flip it back on accept or reject.
Sticky sessions just pin one driver's requests to one instance — coordination still breaks the moment that instance crashes.
Serializing every matching request globally would tank overall throughput, far outweighing the benefit.

scenario: 数据库状态锁配合 Ride Service 内存里的超时定时器来释放锁。
scenario_en: A database state lock relies on an in-memory timer in Ride Service to release the lock on timeout.
q: 数据库状态锁配内存超时释放，还残留什么问题？
q_en: What problem remains with a database state lock plus in-memory timeout release?
options: 服务崩溃或重启后内存定时器丢失，锁可能永远不释放；cron 扫描能兜底但增加复杂度且释放有延迟
数据库因此彻底无法再执行任何一种类型的状态更新操作了
司机客户端会开始持续不断收到大量重复的推送通知消息
事务的隔离级别被设置得不够严格，导致脏读这种现象在高并发场景下变得非常频繁地反复发生
why: 内存超时是易失的：进程一挂定时器就没了，outstanding_request 卡死，这正是内存超时应尽量避免的原因，也是引出 TTL 锁的动机。
why_en: If the service crashes the in-memory timeout vanishes and the lock persists indefinitely, and a cron sweep only adds complexity and delayed unlocking.
options_en: A crash or restart loses the in-memory timer, so the lock may never release; a cron sweep helps but adds complexity and delay.
The database becomes completely unable to execute any type of status update operation anymore.
The driver client starts continuously and repeatedly receiving a flood of duplicate push notifications.
The transaction isolation level is set too loosely, causing dirty reads to happen repeatedly and very frequently under high-concurrency scenarios.
optionExplanations: 对，服务崩溃或重启会让内存定时器一起消失，那个表示司机被占用的状态字段可能永远卡在原地不动；cron 扫描能兜底但会拖慢释放速度、增加运维复杂度。
数据库照样能正常做状态更新，问题出在释放锁的定时器不在数据库里，而在易失的内存中。
重复推送不是这个方案的问题所在，问题是锁可能因为内存定时器丢失而卡住释放不了。
隔离级别不够严格导致脏读是另一类问题，跟内存定时器丢失导致锁卡死没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right, a crash or restart wipes the in-memory timer with it, so the flag marking the driver as taken can stay stuck forever; a cron sweep helps but adds latency and operational complexity.
The database can still update state fine — the problem is that the release timer lives in volatile memory, not in the database.
Repeated pushes aren't the issue here — the issue is the lock getting stuck because the in-memory timer that would release it disappeared.
Loose isolation causing dirty reads is a different class of problem, unrelated to a lock getting stuck from a lost in-memory timer.

scenario: 要保证一个司机同一时刻只收到一个请求，且司机 10 秒不响应后锁必须自动失效，即使服务中途崩溃。
scenario_en: A driver must receive only one request at a time, and the lock must expire automatically after a 10-second silence even if the service crashes.
q: 在这个「必须自动失效」的约束下，最佳锁方案是？
q_en: Under this must-expire-automatically constraint, what is the best lock choice?
options: 数据库里额外加一个状态字段，配合一个专门的 cron 任务定期扫描并清理掉过期的记录
用 ZooKeeper 顺序节点做选主式的长期协调锁定
Redis 分布式锁：key 为 driverId、TTL 设为 10 秒接受窗口，到期自动过期
让客户端 App 自己在本地维护一个倒计时定时器
why: 以 driverId 为 key 获取 Redis 锁并设 10 秒 TTL：抢到锁才能给该司机派单；接受则更新库并释放锁，不响应则锁自动过期、司机重新可用，无需任何内存定时器。
why_en: A Redis distributed lock keyed by driver id with a ten-second TTL auto-expires if the driver ignores the request, surviving service crashes.
whenOtherWins: 规模小、能接受 cron 延迟释放时，纯数据库锁少一个依赖也能用；ZooKeeper 适合长期持有的协调锁而非 10 秒短锁。
tradeoff: 存储层自动过期的可靠性 vs 多一个依赖组件的可用性风险
options_en: Add an extra status field in the database, paired with a dedicated cron job that periodically sweeps and cleans out stale records.
ZooKeeper sequential nodes for leader-election-style long-lived coordination.
A Redis distributed lock keyed by driver id with a ten-second TTL that expires automatically.
Let the client app maintain its own local countdown timer on the device.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键的存活时间，到期后自动被存储层删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a key lives before the storage layer automatically deletes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于共识协议的分布式协调服务，常用于选主和长期锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-based distributed coordination service commonly used for leader election and long-lived locks.

optionExplanations: 数据库字段配 cron 扫描能兜底释放，但释放有延迟，达不到「10 秒必须自动失效」这个硬要求。
ZooKeeper 顺序节点适合长期持有的选主式协调锁，给一把只活 10 秒的短锁用它是杀鸡用牛刀。
对，用司机 ID 当 key 去申请一把 10 秒 TTL 的 Redis 锁，到期后存储层自动释放，不依赖任何进程内定时器。
客户端本地定时器完全不可信，司机 App 可能被杀、离线或被篡改，锁不能交给它管。
optionExplanations_en: A database field with a cron sweep provides eventual release, but with delay — it can't meet the hard 10-second auto-release requirement.
ZooKeeper sequential nodes suit long-held, leader-election-style locks; using it for a lock that only lives 10 seconds is overkill.
Right, take out a Redis lock keyed on the driver's id with a 10-second TTL — the storage layer releases it automatically once it lapses, with no process-internal timer involved.
A client-side local timer isn't trustworthy at all — the driver app can be killed, go offline, or be tampered with, so the lock can't be left to it.

scenario: Redis TTL 锁方案下，司机的响应会走两条完全不同的收尾路径。
scenario_en: Under the Redis TTL lock design, a driver's response follows two different cleanup paths.
q: 司机接受和不响应，分别触发锁的哪种收尾？
q_en: When a driver accepts or does not respond, how should the lock finish?
options: 接受会触发锁的自动续期；不响应时则需要人工介入才能处理
接受会把这把锁转移给乘客持有；不响应则请求直接被判定作废
接受时客户端完全什么都不用做；不响应时这把锁也照样会永久保留在 Redis 里面，不会自动释放掉
接受则更新 ride 为 accepted 并释放锁；不响应则锁到 TTL 自动过期，司机重新可被派单
why: 两条路径都干净收尾：接受即更新状态并释放锁；超时则 TTL 自动过期，匹配服务可把该司机重新纳入候选。
why_en: On acceptance the ride is marked accepted and the lock released, while on timeout the lock simply expires and the driver becomes eligible again.
options_en: Acceptance triggers auto-renewal of the lock; non-response requires manual intervention to handle.
Acceptance transfers the lock over to the rider; non-response voids the request outright.
On acceptance the client does absolutely nothing at all; on non-response the lock likewise just sits in Redis forever and never gets released automatically.
Acceptance marks the ride accepted and releases the lock; non-response lets the TTL expire so the driver is eligible again.
optionExplanations: 接受不会触发续期，不响应也不需要人工介入，两边都是自动化的干净收尾。
锁不会转移给乘客，乘客本来就不持有这把锁；不响应也不是直接判定请求作废，是顺延给下一位司机。
接受这一步其实要更新 ride 状态并释放锁，不是什么都不做；锁也不会永久留存，会自动到期。
对，接受时更新 ride 为 accepted 并主动释放锁；不响应则锁靠 TTL 自动到期，司机重新可被派单。
optionExplanations_en: Acceptance doesn't trigger renewal, and no-response doesn't need manual intervention — both paths resolve automatically.
The lock never transfers to the rider, who never held it in the first place; a no-response doesn't void the request outright either, it just moves to the next driver.
Acceptance actually does update the ride status and release the lock, not nothing; and the lock doesn't sit forever — it lapses on its own.
Right, acceptance updates the ride to accepted and releases the lock; a no-response just lets the TTL lapse on its own, freeing the driver for new dispatch.

scenario: 把派单一致性押在 Redis 锁上之后，系统对锁存储本身产生了新的依赖。
scenario_en: After dispatch consistency depends on Redis locks, the system has a new dependency on the lock store itself.
q: Redis TTL 锁方案的主要挑战是什么，为什么仍是合理权衡？
q_en: What is the main challenge of the Redis TTL lock design, and why is it still a reasonable tradeoff?
options: 锁竞争导致整体系统吞吐骤降，代价完全不可接受
系统依赖内存锁存储的可用性与性能，需要监控与故障转移；但锁只存活 10 秒、数据短命，故障后很容易恢复
TTL 计时天生就不精确，必然会导致重复派单这个问题，所以必须换成 ZooKeeper 才行
Redis 的单线程模型根本无法处理加锁类的请求
why: 新增依赖：派单正确性现在靠 Redis 锁存储在线且够快，需监控+故障转移。但锁只有 10 秒 TTL、数据短命，Redis 挂了锁自然过期重建、恢复很容易——依赖真实但廉价，划算。防重派靠下游 ride 状态校验/fencing，不是锁本身。
why_en: The new dependency is that dispatch correctness now needs the Redis lock store up and fast (monitor + failover). But locks are ephemeral (10s TTL), so a failure self-heals as locks expire and re-form — a real but cheap dependency. Actual duplicate prevention comes from downstream ride-status checks / fencing, not the lock itself.
options_en: Lock contention crashes overall system throughput to a completely unacceptable level.
The system now depends on the lock store's availability and performance, needing monitoring and failover, but the ten-second lock lifetime makes recovery easy.
TTL timing is inherently imprecise and would inevitably cause this duplicate-dispatch problem, so it has to be replaced with ZooKeeper instead.
Redis's single-threaded model is fundamentally unable to process locking requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 原子加锁：仅当 key 不存在时设值(NX)、并带过期(EX)；单线程保证原子，持锁者崩了靠 TTL 自动释放
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SET key val NX EX 10 atomically acquires a lock only if absent, with a TTL so a crashed holder auto-releases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个 worker 抢同一把锁 → 只有一个赢、其余等待、串行化，吞吐下降；细粒度按 key 分锁可避免
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock contention is many workers fighting for the same lock, serializing them; fine-grained per-key locks avoid it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带单调递增编号的令牌；下游存储只接受更大编号的写，从而拒绝「锁已过期的旧持有者」的迟到写
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing number; downstream storage rejects stale-token writes, blocking a holder whose lease expired.

codeSample:
# 加锁：SET NX EX = 原子的「不存在才设 + 10 秒自动过期」
token = uuid()                       # 唯一令牌，只删自己的锁
if SET lock:ride:42 token NX EX 10:  # NX=仅当不存在；EX=10s TTL（崩了也自动释放）
    try:
        do_dispatch(ride 42)         # 临界区：同一 ride 只有一个 matcher 进得来
    finally:
        # 释放：确认是自己的锁再删（Lua 让 check+del 原子）
        EVAL "if GET(KEYS[1])==ARGV[1] then DEL(KEYS[1]) end" 1 lock:ride:42 token
else:
    return   # 没抢到 → 别人在处理，跳过/重试
optionExplanations: 锁竞争不会让系统整体吞吐骤降，这里的锁只针对单个司机、粒度很细。
对，正确性现在建立在锁存储保持在线和低延迟上，需要额外监控与故障转移；但每把锁只活 10 秒、数据短命，出问题也很快能自愈，这份依赖代价可控。
TTL 计时本身够用，误差不至于导致必须换掉整个方案；真正防重派靠下游状态校验，不是靠计时精度。
Redis 单线程模型处理加锁类命令效率很高，不是短板，这不是这里的挑战。
optionExplanations_en: Lock contention wouldn't tank overall system throughput — each lock is scoped to a single driver, so it's fine-grained.

Right, correctness now rests on the lock store staying up and fast, which needs extra monitoring and failover; but since each lock only lives 10 seconds, recovery after trouble is quick and the dependency stays cheap.
TTL timing is precise enough on its own; the real guard against double-dispatch is the downstream ride-status check, not timer precision.
Redis's single-threaded model actually handles locking commands efficiently — that's not the weak point here.

q: 把「司机派单一致性」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the driver dispatch consistency decision chain in the correct order:
steps: 选型：Redis 分布式锁，key=driverId、TTL=10 秒
缓解：接受则更新状态并释放锁；超时则锁自动过期、司机重新可用
需求：匹配强一致——一个司机同一时刻只能有一个待处理请求，10 秒响应窗口
代价：正确性依赖内存锁存储的可用性与性能
why: 链条：一个司机同一时刻只能锁给一个请求的需求，推出 Redis TTL 锁这个选型，暴露出依赖锁存储可用性的代价，最后用干净的接受/超时两条路径收尾缓解。
why_en: The one-driver-one-request requirement leads to a Redis TTL lock, which trades in a dependency on the lock store's availability, mitigated by clean accept and timeout paths.
diagram:
graph TD
    Need[One driver per ride] --> Choice[Redis TTL lock]
    Choice --> Cost[Depends on lock store availability]
    Cost --> Mitigate[Accept releases; timeout auto-expires]

scenario: 对比数据库状态锁和 Redis TTL 锁这两种方案在「超时释放」这一个维度上的差别。
scenario_en: Compare database state locks and Redis TTL locks on the single dimension of timeout release.
q: 在超时释放这个维度上，数据库状态锁与 Redis TTL 锁的区别是？
q_en: On timeout release, how do database state locks and Redis TTL locks differ?
options: 数据库锁靠易失的内存定时器或 cron 兜底释放；Redis 锁由 TTL 自动过期，天然抗服务崩溃
两者都能在到期后自动过期释放，二者之间没有任何实质差别
Redis 锁反而还额外需要单独配一个 cron 任务来做兜底保障，数据库锁则完全不需要
两者都要依赖客户端主动调用一个专门的释放接口才能解锁
why: 关键差异在释放机制：数据库锁的释放逻辑活在应用进程里，崩溃即丢；Redis 把过期下沉到存储层，进程崩溃不影响。
why_en: A database lock relies on fragile in-memory timers or cron sweeps to release, while a Redis lock expires automatically via TTL even if the service crashes.
tradeoff: 释放机制活在应用进程里 vs 释放机制下沉到存储层
options_en: A database lock relies on fragile in-memory timers or cron sweeps, while a Redis lock auto-expires via TTL and survives crashes.
Both auto-expire on schedule with absolutely no real difference between the two.
The Redis lock is actually the one that additionally needs a separate extra cron job as a backstop guarantee, while the database lock needs none at all.
Both require the client to explicitly call a dedicated release endpoint to unlock.

rows: 定时器丢失，锁可能悬挂
存储层 TTL 自动过期

optionExplanations: 对，数据库锁靠应用进程里的内存定时器或 cron 兜底释放，进程一崩就丢；Redis 把这份职责放进了它自己的存储引擎，进程崩溃完全不受影响。
两者在超时释放上差别很大：一个释放逻辑活在应用进程里，一个下沉到存储层，稳健程度完全不同。
恰恰相反，需要额外配 cron 兜底的是数据库锁方案，Redis TTL 本身就能自动到期。
两种锁的自动释放都不依赖客户端主动调用接口，靠的是各自的过期机制。
optionExplanations_en: Right, a database lock relies on a memory timer or cron running inside the app process, so a crash loses it; Redis keeps that responsibility inside its own storage engine, unaffected by process crashes.
The two differ a lot on timeout release: one lives in the app process, the other sits in the storage layer — very different robustness.
It's the opposite — the database-lock approach is the one that needs an extra cron backstop; Redis's TTL already lapses on its own.
Neither approach's auto-release depends on the client calling an endpoint — both rely on their own timeout mechanism.

scenario: 当前设计「裸奔」：既没有队列削峰、也没有限流 / 降载保护，请求来了就同步处理（FCFS）。评估这个无保护基线在流量峰值时的表现。
scenario_en: The current design is unprotected: no queue to absorb bursts and no rate limiting / load shedding — incoming requests are handled synchronously (FCFS). Evaluate this baseline at peak traffic.
q: 不加队列、同步处理请求，在峰值会发生什么？
q_en: What happens at peak if requests are processed synchronously with no queue?
options: 只是整个系统的平均延迟出现了一点点小幅上升而已，完全不会影响到系统整体的正确性表现
系统会在流量峰值时自动降级切换成批处理模式运行
突发流量下系统过载开始丢请求；实例崩溃时在途请求全部丢失，乘客无限等待一个永远不来的匹配
会导致数据库层面产生大量难以排查的死锁问题
why: 既无缓冲又无保护：峰值下线程/连接耗尽、延迟飙升，请求超时失败——这是「过载崩溃式丢」，不是限流那种干净拒绝；实例挂掉在途请求还无恢复。修法=加队列削峰（或限流/降载），见后续卡。
why_en: No buffer, no protection: a surge exhausts the service and requests fail by timeout — ungraceful overload collapse, not a clean rate-limit 429; a crash also loses in-flight matches. Fix: add a queue (or rate limiting / load shedding).
options_en: Only the system's overall average latency ticks up a small amount, with no impact whatsoever on the system's overall correctness.
The system automatically degrades and switches into batch mode at peak traffic.
Surges overwhelm the system and drop requests; a crash loses every in-flight request with riders waiting on a match that never comes.
It causes a large number of hard-to-debug deadlocks at the database layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动机制：超过设定速率就直接拒绝多余请求（通常返回 429「请求过多」）；防滥用/配额，不是过载时的被动崩溃
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limiter proactively rejects requests above a set rate (usually HTTP 429) — protection against abuse/quotas, not passive overload collapse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统不健康时主动丢弃部分请求以自保，比过载崩溃式丢更可控
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding deliberately drops some requests when the system is unhealthy, to protect it — more controlled than a collapse.

optionExplanations: 这不只是延迟小幅上升，而是线程连接被耗尽后请求直接超时失败。
系统不会自动切成批处理模式，没有队列缓冲这条路根本不存在。
对，突发流量下线程连接耗尽、请求超时丢失；实例一旦崩溃在途请求也没有持久化，乘客等到的是永远不会来的匹配。
同步处理请求跟数据库死锁没有直接因果关系，这不是这里的失败模式。
optionExplanations_en: This isn't a slight latency bump — threads and connections get exhausted and requests time out outright.
The system doesn't auto-degrade into a batch mode — there's no queue buffer for it to fall back on.

Right, under a burst, threads and connections exhaust and requests fail on timeout; if an instance crashes, in-flight requests are never persisted, so the rider waits forever for a match that never comes.
Synchronous processing has no direct causal link to database deadlocks — that's not the failure mode here.

scenario: 演唱会散场，同一地点瞬间涌入 10 万级乘车请求；不允许丢单，且匹配实例可能随时崩溃或重启。
scenario_en: After a concert ends, about 100k ride requests arrive at one location at once; requests cannot be dropped, and matching instances may crash or restart.
q: 在这个不允许丢单的约束下，怎么改造匹配入口？
q_en: Under this no-lost-requests constraint, how should the matching entry point change?
options: 把匹配服务垂直扩容到市面上当前能够买到的最高规格硬件配置上去，别的都先不考虑
让客户端自己实现一套指数退避式的请求重试逻辑
对超出容量上限的请求直接做限流并拒绝处理
请求先进消息队列，匹配服务按序消费；按队列长度动态扩容消费者，并可按地理区域分区
why: 队列把突发流量削峰缓存下来，消费者按需横向扩容保证不丢单；按地域分区进一步提升效率。
why_en: A queue buffers surge demand while matching consumers scale out dynamically, and partitioning by region keeps processing efficient.
whenOtherWins: 平稳低负载、对首跳延迟极敏感时，直接同步处理更简单；队列的运维复杂度可用托管服务缓解。
tradeoff: 不丢单的缓冲能力 vs 引入队列的额外延迟和运维
options_en: Scale the matching service vertically up to whatever the highest-spec hardware configuration is currently available to buy, and set everything else aside.
Have the client implement its own exponential-backoff retry logic.
Rate-limit and outright reject requests that exceed the current capacity ceiling.
Put requests into a queue first; matching consumers scale out based on queue depth and can partition by region.
optionExplanations: 垂直扩容到顶配硬件终究有物理上限，遇到演唱会散场这种量级还是会被打穿。
客户端自己退避重试解决不了服务端积压，请求照样在服务端排队等着被处理。
限流拒绝正好违反「不允许丢单」的约束，这里要的是缓冲而不是拒绝。
对，请求先进队列削峰，消费者按队列长度动态扩容，还能按地域分区，既不丢单又能扛住突发。
optionExplanations_en: Scaling vertically to the biggest box available still hits a physical ceiling — a stadium-crowd-sized burst would blow through it anyway.
Client-side backoff retries don't relieve server-side backlog — the requests are still queued up waiting to be processed there.
Rate-limiting and rejecting directly violates the no-dropped-orders constraint here — the need is buffering, not rejection.
Right, requests land in a queue that absorbs the burst, consumers scale with queue length, and partitioning by geography adds further headroom — no drops, and it survives the spike.

scenario: 用 Kafka 这个分布式消息队列承接乘车请求，要求匹配实例崩溃也不能丢单。
scenario_en: Kafka is used as the distributed queue for ride requests, and matching instances must not lose requests when they crash.
q: 用 Kafka 做请求队列时，怎么保证匹配实例崩溃也不丢单？
q_en: How does Kafka keep ride requests from being lost when a matching instance crashes?
options: 匹配成功后才提交消息 offset，崩溃时消息仍在队列里，新实例会重新消费
消费者一读到消息，就立即同步提交 offset，然后才开始处理
把每条消息在生产端复制成三份分别发送出去
完全依赖生产者不断重发消息来做兜底保证
why: 偏移量在成功找到匹配后才提交：处理中崩溃则 offset 未动，消息对新实例仍然可见，系统天然获得故障容错。
why_en: Committing the Kafka offset only after a successful match means a crashed instance leaves the request in the queue for another instance to pick up.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["请求写入队列 按地域分区"] --> B["匹配服务消费"]
    B --> C{"匹配成功?"}
    C -- "是" --> D["提交 offset"]
    C -- "实例崩溃" --> E["offset 未提交 消息仍在 新实例接手"]
options_en: Commit the message offset only after a successful match, so a crash leaves the message in the queue for a new instance to pick up.
The moment the consumer reads the message, it synchronously commits the offset, and only then starts processing.
Have the producer send three separate copies of every message.
Rely entirely on the producer continuously resending messages as a backstop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式的发布订阅消息队列，靠分区和偏移量管理消费进度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed publish-subscribe message queue that tracks consumer progress with partitions and offsets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者在某个分区里读到的位置标记，提交后表示这之前的消息已处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the marker of how far a consumer has read in a partition; committing it means everything before is processed.

optionExplanations: 对，只有匹配成功才提交 offset，处理中途崩溃 offset 没动，消息对新实例依然可见，天然获得容错。
读到消息就立刻提交 offset，处理中途一崩，消息就被标记已消费而实际没处理完，等于丢单。
生产端多副本能防 broker 故障丢消息，但防不住消费者处理中途崩溃导致的丢单。
完全靠生产者重发没有触发重发的信号，消费者处理失败并不会告诉生产者去重发。
optionExplanations_en: Right, the offset only commits after a successful match; if processing crashes mid-way, the offset never moved, so the message stays visible to a new instance — fault tolerance for free.
Committing the offset the instant it's read, before processing, means a mid-processing crash leaves the message marked consumed even though it never finished — a silent loss.
Replicating on the producer side guards against broker failure, not against a consumer crashing mid-processing.
Relying purely on producer resend has no trigger — a consumer's processing failure doesn't signal the producer to resend anything.

scenario: 请求队列按地理区域切分成多个分区，而不是全局一个分区。
scenario_en: The request queue is partitioned by geographic region rather than kept as one global partition.
q: 为什么把请求队列按地理区域分区？
q_en: Why partition the request queue by geographic region?
options: 单纯是为了满足某种数据合规方面的要求
匹配天然只关心同区域的司机与乘客，按地域分区能提升处理效率
只是为了让单条消息体积在传输时变得更小
Kafka 这个消息队列本身强制要求必须做分区
why: 叫车匹配是强地域局部的：旧金山的请求不需要和纽约的抢同一个队列。按区域分区提升吞吐，也为地理分片铺路。
why_en: Ride matching is inherently local, so partitioning queues by geographic region improves processing efficiency.
options_en: Purely to satisfy some data compliance requirement.
Matching is inherently local, so regional partitioning improves processing efficiency.
Just to make each individual message body smaller in transit.
The Kafka message queue itself mandates that partitioning be used.
optionExplanations: 分区跟数据合规没关系，这里纯粹是为了匹配效率的架构决定。
对，匹配天然只看同区域的司机和乘客，旧金山的请求不需要跟纽约的抢同一个队列，按地域分区提升处理效率。
分区不会改变单条消息本身的体积，跟消息大小无关。
Kafka 本身不强制要求按地域分区，是否分区、怎么分是团队自己的架构决定。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning has nothing to do with data compliance — this is purely an architectural decision for matching efficiency.
Right, matching is inherently regional — a San Francisco request never needs to compete for the same queue as a New York one — so partitioning by region improves throughput.
Partitioning doesn't shrink any individual message's size, unrelated to message size.
Kafka itself doesn't force geo partitioning — whether and how to partition is the team's own architectural call.

scenario: 团队不想自己运维高可用、可扩展的队列基础设施。
scenario_en: The team does not want to operate highly available, scalable queue infrastructure itself.
q: 不想自己运维队列基础设施，可以选用什么？
q_en: What can you use if you do not want to operate queue infrastructure yourself?
options: 自己从零开始搭建并长期运维一整套完整的 ZooKeeper 加 Kafka 集群
直接把队列语义借助 Redis list 数据结构自己实现
托管服务：Amazon SQS、Amazon MSK 或 Confluent Cloud
用一张普通数据库表来模拟队列的入队和出队操作
why: 托管队列服务开箱提供扩展性、容错和高可用，团队可以专注业务逻辑而不是队列基础设施。
why_en: Managed services like Amazon SQS, MSK, or Confluent Cloud provide scalable, fault-tolerant queues out of the box.
options_en: Build an entire complete ZooKeeper-plus-Kafka cluster from scratch and operate it long-term all by yourself.
Implement queue semantics yourself on top of a Redis list data structure.
Use a managed service such as Amazon SQS, Amazon MSK, or Confluent Cloud.
Simulate enqueue and dequeue operations with an ordinary database table.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的全托管消息队列服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS is AWS's fully managed message queue service.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的全托管 Kafka 服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSK is AWS's fully managed Apache Kafka service.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 商业公司 Confluent 提供的全托管 Kafka 云服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Confluent Cloud is a fully managed Kafka service run by Confluent, the company founded by Kafka's creators.

optionExplanations: 从零自建 ZooKeeper 加 Kafka 集群正是团队想避免的运维负担，跟不想自己运维的诉求矛盾。
用 Redis list 模拟队列语义要自己补全消费确认、重试、扩展等一整套能力，运维负担并没有真正减少。
对，SQS、MSK、Confluent Cloud 这类托管服务开箱就有扩展性、容错和高可用，团队专注业务逻辑就够了。
用普通数据库表模拟队列的入队出队，在这个写入量级下性能和扩展性都跟不上。
optionExplanations_en: Self-hosting a ZooKeeper-plus-Kafka cluster from scratch is exactly the operational burden the team wants to avoid — it contradicts the goal.
Faking queue semantics with a Redis list still means building consumer acks, retries, and scaling yourself — the ops burden doesn't actually go away.
Right, managed services like SQS, MSK, or Confluent Cloud give you scalability, fault tolerance, and high availability out of the box, so the team can focus on business logic.
Simulating enqueue/dequeue with an ordinary database table can't keep up in performance or scale at this write volume.

scenario: 请求队列目前是纯 FIFO，一个难匹配的请求可能挡住后面所有请求。
scenario_en: The request queue is pure FIFO, and one hard-to-match request can block every request behind it.
q: FIFO 队列在匹配场景里有什么问题，怎么应对？
q_en: What is the problem with FIFO queues in matching, and how do you handle it?
options: FIFO 天然公平，在这个匹配场景里完全没有问题
处理慢的请求会堵住后面的请求（队头阻塞），改用优先队列按邻近度、评分等因素优先处理
FIFO 队列本身就会丢消息，所以理应改用后进先出的 FILO 队列才对
FIFO 处理吞吐太快，反而会把下游服务直接压垮
why: 一个难匹配的请求可能卡住整队。优先队列按邻近度、评分等因素调度，让最该先处理的请求先出队，改善整体体验。
why_en: A slow request can block a FIFO queue, so a priority queue ordered by factors like proximity and rating processes the most important requests first.
options_en: FIFO is inherently fair, so there's absolutely no problem in this matching scenario.
A slow request causes head-of-line blocking; switch to a priority queue ordered by proximity, rating, and similar factors.
Plain FIFO queues inherently drop messages on their own, so it really ought to be replaced with a last-in-first-out FILO queue.
FIFO's processing throughput is too fast and ends up crushing downstream services.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出的处理顺序，消息按到达顺序被消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO processes messages in the order they arrived, first in and first out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队首一条处理慢的消息挡住后面全部消息被消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Head-of-line blocking is when one slow message at the front of a queue delays everything behind it.

optionExplanations: FIFO 公平但不智能，一个难匹配的请求会卡住后面所有请求，这正是问题所在。
对，纯 FIFO 会出现队头阻塞，换成按邻近度、评分等因素排序的调度，让最该先处理的请求先出队。
FIFO 本身不丢消息，问题出在处理顺序而不是消息丢失，换成后进先出也解决不了阻塞。
FIFO 吞吐太快压垮下游不是这里描述的问题，问题是慢请求挡住后面的请求。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO is fair but not smart — a hard-to-match request blocks everything behind it, which is exactly the problem here.
Right, plain FIFO causes head-of-line blocking; switching to scheduling ranked by proximity, rating, and similar factors lets the requests that matter most go first.
FIFO itself doesn't drop messages — the issue is processing order, not loss, and switching to last-in-first-out wouldn't fix blocking either.
FIFO overwhelming downstream with speed isn't the problem described here — the problem is a slow request blocking the ones behind it.

scenario: 把新订单推给司机属于系统设计里常见的「服务端主动推送」场景。
scenario_en: Pushing a new order to the driver is a common server-initiated update scenario in system design.
q: 除了系统推送 APNs/FCM，服务端向客户端推送还有哪些经典选项？
q_en: Besides APNs/FCM, what classic options exist for server-to-client push?
options: 从长轮询（long-polling）到 SSE 再到 WebSocket 这一整条能力递进谱
只能依靠 FTP 这种老式文件传输协议和 SMTP 这种电子邮件协议，别无其他任何选择
只能靠客户端定时发起短轮询请求这一种办法可用
只能靠 UDP 组播广播这种无连接的方式来实现
why: 给司机的实时派单属于实时更新 pattern：从长轮询到 SSE 再到 WebSocket，是一条推送能力递进的选项谱。
why_en: Real-time server pushes range from long-polling to server-sent events to WebSockets.
options_en: The full capability spectrum from long-polling to server-sent events to WebSocket.
The only options are these old-school protocols: FTP for file transfer and SMTP for email, with absolutely nothing else available.
The only available approach is periodic client-side short polling requests.
The only option is a connectionless UDP multicast broadcast mechanism.

rows: 更新不频繁、兼容性优先
服务端到客户端单向长连接

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端反复发起请求，服务端有数据才响应、没有则挂起等待的推送方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long-polling has the client repeatedly request updates while the server holds the connection open until there is new data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端到客户端的单向持续推送通道，基于 HTTP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is a one-way, persistent server-to-client push channel built on HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务端之间的全双工长连接协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a full-duplex, persistent connection protocol between client and server.

optionExplanations: 对，从最基础的轮询方式一路进化到 SSE、再到 WebSocket，是服务端推送能力由弱到强的一条谱系。
FTP 和 SMTP 是文件传输和邮件协议，都不是为服务端主动推送实时更新设计的。
定时短轮询能凑合实现推送效果，但它只是这条谱系里最弱的一端，不是唯一选项。
UDP 组播适合一对多广播场景，不是给单个司机做可靠实时推送的经典选项。
optionExplanations_en: Right, evolving from basic polling up through SSE and then WebSocket forms a spectrum of increasingly capable server-push mechanisms.
FTP and SMTP are file-transfer and email protocols, neither designed for active server-initiated real-time push.
Timed short polling can crudely fake push, but it's just the weakest end of that spectrum, not the only option.
UDP multicast suits one-to-many broadcast scenarios, not the classic choice for reliable real-time push to a single driver.

scenario: 司机响应超时后自动顺延到下一位，这类「人在环节中」的多步流程有一个和 Uber 相关的历史渊源。
scenario_en: Automatically moving to the next driver after a timeout is a human-in-the-loop multi-step workflow with a historical link to Uber.
q: Uber 与「人在环节中」的多步流程调度框架有什么历史渊源？
q_en: What is Uber's historical connection to human-in-the-loop multi-step workflow frameworks?
options: Uber 一直只使用完全闭源、从不开源的自研调度器
其实是 Airbnb 团队最早发明出来并率先把 Temporal 这个框架开源的
这类人在环节中的问题在业界只能靠 cron 定时任务硬解决
Uber 是开源项目 Cadence 的原作者，它催生了主流持久执行框架 Temporal
why: 司机响应这类 human-in-the-loop 流程是多步流程 pattern 的典型信号；Uber 开源的 Cadence 正是 Temporal 的前身，专为此类场景而生。
why_en: Uber authored the open-source Cadence project, which gave birth to Temporal, the leading durable execution framework for exactly these human-in-the-loop workflows.
options_en: Uber has always used a fully closed-source, never open-sourced in-house scheduler.
It was actually the Airbnb team that first invented it and was the first to open-source the Temporal framework.
This class of human-in-the-loop problem can only be brute-forced with cron jobs.
Uber authored the open-source Cadence project, which gave birth to the leading durable execution framework Temporal.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的持久执行工作流引擎，是 Temporal 的前身。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cadence is Uber's open-source durable execution workflow engine, the predecessor of Temporal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流程中某一步需要等待人类（这里是司机）响应才能继续的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Human-in-the-loop describes a workflow step that must wait on a human response, here the driver, before proceeding.

optionExplanations: Uber 恰恰把这类调度器开源了，Cadence 项目公开且被业界广泛使用。
开源并催生 Temporal 前身的是 Uber 的 Cadence 项目，不是 Airbnb。
这类人在环节中的多步流程业界早有专门的持久执行框架，不是只能靠 cron 硬扛。
对，Uber 是 Cadence 的原作者并将其开源，Cadence 正是主流持久执行框架 Temporal 的前身。
optionExplanations_en: Uber actually open-sourced this kind of scheduler — the Cadence project is public and widely adopted.
It was Uber's Cadence project that was open-sourced and became Temporal's precursor, not Airbnb.
This class of human-in-the-loop, multi-step flow already has dedicated durable-execution frameworks — it isn't limited to brute-forcing it with cron.
Right, Uber authored and open-sourced Cadence, which became the precursor to the mainstream durable-execution framework Temporal.

scenario: 司机把手机丢在副驾没看到派单，10 秒窗口静默流逝；系统必须自动把请求转给下一位候选司机。
scenario_en: A driver misses the dispatch because the phone is out of sight, and the 10-second window passes silently; the system must automatically try the next candidate.
q: 用队列原语怎么实现「超时自动顺延给下一位司机」？
q_en: How can queue primitives implement timeout and move to the next driver?
options: 在乘客客户端弹出一个对话框窗口，让用户自己手动点击重试按钮再来一次
派单的同时向延迟队列投一条 10 秒后可见的消息；到期若 ride 仍未分配，就发给下一位司机并再投一条延迟消息
每秒钟都要对整张 ride 数据表完完整整地做一次全表扫描，一行一行仔细找出所有仍然未分配的记录才行
一次性把这条请求同时群发给排名前 10 位的全部候选司机们
why: 延迟消息=那个「计时器」：派单时就投一条 10 秒后可见的消息（没有别的时钟会告诉你超时，所以要提前投）。到期它只是触发器，worker 先查 ride 状态：已接受→丢弃(幂等无害)；仍未分配→顺延下一位并续投。热状态放 Redis 查得快，最终分配落 DB。
why_en: The delayed message is the timer — schedule it at offer time, not after. When it fires it just triggers a check: if the ride is already taken, discard it (idempotent); if not, offer the next driver and reschedule. Keep the hot status in Redis, persist the assignment in the DB.
whenOtherWins: 流程更复杂或不容出错时，用 Temporal/Step Functions 这类持久执行框架，内建超时重试与状态管理，比手工管理延迟消息更稳。
tradeoff: 延迟队列实现简单 vs 持久执行框架的健壮性与内建状态管理
options_en: Pop up a dialog box on the rider's client and let the user manually click a retry button to try again.
Alongside each offer, schedule a delayed message visible after ten seconds; if the ride is still unassigned when it fires, offer the next driver and schedule another delayed message.
Every single second, run a completely full scan across the entire ride table, checking row by row to find every record that's still unassigned.
Broadcast the request simultaneously to all of the top ten ranked candidate drivers at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息发布后延迟一段时间才对消费者可见的队列机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delay queue holds a message invisible to consumers until a set delay elapses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作执行一次或多次结果相同；这里靠「到期先查状态」保证重复触发也无害
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means repeating the operation has the same effect — re-checking status on fire makes duplicate triggers harmless.

optionExplanations: 让乘客自己点重试没有解决司机端超时顺延这件事，责任放错了对象。
对，派单同时投一条 10 秒后可见的延迟消息当计时器，到期先查 ride 状态，仍未分配才顺延给下一位并再投一条延迟消息。
每秒全表扫描找未分配行程，规模一大就是巨大的数据库开销，代价远高于一条延迟消息。
一次性群发前 10 位候选司机，会让多个司机同时被同一单占用，破坏一次只锁一个人的一致性要求。
optionExplanations_en: Having the rider manually click retry doesn't address driver-side timeout escalation — it puts the responsibility on the wrong party.

Right, dispatch also enqueues a message that becomes visible in 10 seconds as the "timer"; when it comes due, it checks the ride status first and only escalates to the next driver, requeuing another delayed message, if it's still unassigned.
Scanning the whole table every second for unassigned rides is a massive database cost at scale, far worse than one delayed message.
Broadcasting to the top 10 candidates at once lets multiple drivers get tied up by the same request, breaking the one-driver-at-a-time consistency rule.

scenario: 延迟消息到期后触发处理逻辑，但司机可能已经在到期前接单了。
scenario_en: A delayed message fires and triggers processing, but the driver may have accepted before the timeout.
q: 延迟消息到期被处理时，系统首先要检查什么？
q_en: What should the system check first when a delayed message fires?
options: 先检查司机的历史评分是否达到平台标准
先检查一下这条延迟消息是不是跟之前已经投递过的某一条重复了才对
该 ride 是否仍未被分配，已分配则忽略，仍未分配才转给下一位司机
先检查乘客客户端此刻是否还保持在线状态
why: 到期消息只是「可能超时」的信号：先查 ride 状态，仍未分配才顺延到下一位司机，避免把已分配的行程错误重派。
why_en: When the delayed message fires, the system first checks whether the ride is still unassigned before moving on to the next driver.
options_en: First check whether the driver's historical rating meets the platform's bar.
First check whether this delayed message duplicates one that was already enqueued earlier before doing anything else at all.
Whether the ride is still unassigned; if already assigned, ignore it, otherwise move to the next driver.
First check whether the rider's client is currently online.
optionExplanations: 司机评分是匹配阶段用的排序因素，跟延迟消息到期后要不要顺延没关系。
延迟消息本身不需要去重判断，问题是它到期时行程可能已经被接受了。
对，延迟消息到期只是「可能超时」的信号，先查 ride 是否仍未分配，仍未分配才顺延到下一位。
乘客是否在线不影响司机是否已经接单这件事，检查点应该在 ride 状态而不是乘客连接。
optionExplanations_en: Driver rating is a ranking factor used during matching, unrelated to whether a due delayed message should escalate.
The delayed message itself doesn't need dedup — the real issue is that the ride may already be accepted by the time it comes due.
Right, a due delayed message is only a "possibly timed out" signal — it checks whether the ride is still unassigned before escalating to the next driver.
Whether the rider is online has no bearing on whether the driver already accepted — the check belongs on ride status, not rider connectivity.

scenario: 司机在延迟消息已经排定、但还没被处理的窗口期内接了单。
scenario_en: The driver accepts during the window after the delayed message is scheduled but before it is processed.
q: 延迟队列方案的主要挑战是什么？
q_en: What is the main challenge of the delayed-queue design?
options: 司机在延迟消息排定但未处理时接单，要保证延迟消息被优雅取消或忽略，且延迟队列与匹配服务之间要小心协调防竞态
延迟消息存在一个理论上已经被严格证明是完全无法解决的时钟漂移问题，会让所有的计时都彻底失准报废掉
SQS 这类主流的托管队列服务根本就完全不支持延迟消息这项功能特性
运行并维护一整套延迟队列基础设施的成本高到团队完全无法承受
why: 延迟消息是派单时就定好的定时器；在它到期前司机可能已接单 →「接单」和「超时重派」两操作撞车（竞态），不协调就可能一单派俩司机。修法：超时先校验 ride 状态+幂等（已接受就忽略），状态变更走原子 CAS/锁，让两者只有一个赢。
why_en: The timeout can fire just as the driver accepts, so accept and timeout-reassign race — uncoordinated, one ride could go to two drivers. Fix: the timeout re-checks status and is idempotent, and status changes use an atomic CAS/lock so only one wins.
options_en: A driver accepting while the delayed message is pending requires it to be gracefully canceled or ignored, and the two components must coordinate carefully to avoid races.
Delayed messages suffer a clock-drift problem that has been rigorously proven theoretically unsolvable, throwing all timing completely off and useless.
Mainstream managed queue services like SQS supposedly don't support delayed messages as a feature at all.
The cost of running and maintaining an entire delay-queue infrastructure is more than the team can bear.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个并发操作交错执行导致结果不一致；这里是「接单」和「超时重派」同时发生互相撞
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is when two concurrent operations interleave into an inconsistent result — here, accept vs timeout-reassign.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子操作：只有当前值等于预期时才更新，否则失败——用它让状态变更只有一个赢家
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set atomically updates only if the value still equals the expected one, so only one racing writer wins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作执行一次或多次结果相同；超时处理器「已接受就忽略」就是幂等
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means repeating an operation has the same effect — the timeout handler no-ops if already accepted.

optionExplanations: 对，司机可能在延迟消息排定但没到期前就接单了，「接单」和「超时重派」这两个动作可能撞车，不协调好就可能一单派给两个司机。
时钟漂移是可以工程上缓解的问题，不是这里真正卡住的挑战。
SQS 本身是支持延迟消息的，问题不在于工具能力缺失。
运维延迟队列基础设施的成本在这个规模下是可以接受的，不是这里的主要挑战。
optionExplanations_en: Right, a driver can accept before the delayed message comes due, so "accept" and "timeout escalate" can race — without coordination, one ride could get dispatched to two drivers.
Clock drift is an engineering problem that can be mitigated, not the real blocker here.
SQS does support delayed messages, so tooling capability isn't the gap.
The operational cost of running delayed-queue infrastructure is affordable at this scale — that's not the main challenge here.

scenario: 匹配是一个多步、含超时重试、逐个降级候选司机的流程；服务可能崩溃重启，但流程状态绝不能丢。
scenario_en: Matching is a multi-step flow with timeouts, retries, and candidate fallback; services may crash and restart, but workflow state must not be lost.
q: 在流程状态绝不能丢的约束下，最健壮的实现方式是？
q_en: Under the constraint that workflow state must never be lost, what is the most robust implementation?
options: SQS 延迟消息，再配合团队自己手写并且需要长期持续维护的取消逻辑代码
把整个流程的状态完完全全放在服务实例自己这一个进程的内存里面去，用一个状态机对象统一维护管理起来才行
用 Temporal/Step Functions 等持久执行框架把匹配建模成持久工作流，崩溃后自动从断点恢复
把整个流程状态直接以明文形式存放在司机手机的本地存储里
why: 持久执行框架把整个工作流状态持久化：服务崩溃、网络故障都不会丢状态或丢请求，超时和降级逻辑都是框架原语。
why_en: A durable execution framework like Temporal models matching as a persistent workflow with built-in timeouts and retries that survives service crashes.
whenOtherWins: 简单流程用延迟队列就够，还省掉新框架的学习与运维成本；持久执行的价值体现在复杂、不容有失的关键路径。
tradeoff: 内建容错与状态持久化 vs 引入新框架的学习和运维成本
options_en: SQS delayed messages, paired with hand-written cancellation logic the team has to maintain indefinitely.
Keep the entire workflow state completely inside this one service instance's own process memory, all maintained together as a single state machine object.
Use a durable execution framework like Temporal or Step Functions to model matching as a persistent workflow that auto-resumes from a checkpoint after a crash.
Store the entire workflow state as plaintext directly in local storage on the driver's phone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源的持久执行工作流引擎，内建超时、重试和状态持久化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is an open-source durable execution workflow engine with built-in timeouts, retries, and state persistence.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管工作流编排服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS Step Functions is AWS's managed workflow orchestration service.

optionExplanations: SQS 延迟消息配自己维护的取消逻辑能跑，但状态还是散落在应用代码里，崩溃后未必能干净恢复，长期维护成本也高。
状态放在服务实例自己的内存对象里，实例一崩溃流程状态就跟着没了，达不到「流程状态绝不能丢」的要求。
对，Temporal/Step Functions 把整条工作流状态持久化在框架里，服务崩溃重启后能直接从断点恢复，超时和降级都是框架原语。
把流程状态明文存在司机手机本地，司机可能卸载 App 或换设备，状态一样会丢失且不可信。
optionExplanations_en: SQS delay messages with hand-maintained cancel logic can work, but state still lives scattered across application code, isn't guaranteed to recover cleanly after a crash, and costs more to maintain long-term.
Keeping state in the service instance's own in-memory object means a crash wipes the workflow state with it, failing the "must never lose flow state" requirement.
Right, Temporal/Step Functions persist the entire workflow state inside the framework, so a crash and restart resumes right from the checkpoint, with timeout and escalation as built-in primitives.
Storing flow state in plaintext on the driver's phone is fragile — the driver could uninstall the app or switch devices, losing or corrupting that state.

scenario: 把司机匹配建模成一个 Temporal 持久工作流后，流程按固定步骤循环推进。
scenario_en: After driver matching is modeled as a Temporal durable workflow, the flow advances through fixed repeated steps.
q: 补全 Temporal 匹配工作流的步骤：
q_en: Fill in the Temporal matching workflow steps:
text: 把请求发给排序第一的司机 → 设 {{10}} 秒超时 → 司机接受则{{完成}}工作流 → 拒绝或超时则自动转给{{下一位}}司机 → 循环直到匹配成功或候选司机{{耗尽}}。
why: 整个流程容错：状态持久化在工作流引擎里，服务故障、网络抖动都不会丢状态或丢单。
why_en: The workflow offers the ride to each driver in turn with a ten-second timeout, completing on acceptance and continuing until a driver is found or the list is exhausted.
diagram:
graph LR
    Start[Ride request] --> Candidates[Rank candidates]
    Candidates --> Offer[Offer driver]
    Offer --> Timer[Wait with timeout]
    Timer -->|decline or timeout| Offer
    Timer -->|accept| Complete[Ride accepted]

scenario: 为匹配流程引入 Temporal 这类工作流编排框架，会带来新的组织和运维成本。
scenario_en: Introducing a workflow orchestration framework such as Temporal for matching adds new organizational and operational cost.
q: 引入 Temporal 等工作流编排的代价是什么，为何通常仍值得？
q_en: What is the cost of introducing Temporal-style workflow orchestration, and why is it usually worth it?
options: 运行成本会直接翻上整整一倍，无论如何都完全不值得引入这套东西
会明显拖慢整体的匹配处理速度，只适合放进那种对时延完全不敏感的离线批处理任务里去用
几乎不会产生任何值得一提的额外代价，团队完完全全可以毫无任何顾虑地在任何时候都直接引入这整套方案来长期使用
团队要学新概念工具、系统多一个要监控维护的组件；但对派单这种掉单直接损失营收的关键系统，保证执行加内建容错通常物超所值
why: 代价是复杂度：新工具、新概念、新的运维面。但换来保证执行、内建容错和更简单的业务逻辑，对营收关键的叫车流程是划算的。
why_en: Durable execution adds tooling complexity and another component to operate, but guaranteed execution usually outweighs that for revenue-critical matching.
options_en: Running costs simply double outright, making it not worth adopting this under any circumstance.
It would noticeably slow down the overall matching processing speed, so it only fits offline batch jobs that are completely insensitive to latency at all.
It adds almost nothing worth mentioning in extra cost at all, so the team can adopt and keep using this whole approach directly at any time whatsoever with absolutely zero hesitation.
The team must learn new tools and operate one more monitored component, but guaranteed execution and built-in fault tolerance usually pay off for revenue-critical dispatch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工作流编排 / 持久化执行引擎：把多步长流程写成代码，自动记住进度，崩溃后从断点精确恢复，内建重试/超时/补偿。源自 Uber 内部的 Cadence，不是 AI agent 专用框架
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is a durable-execution / workflow engine that runs multi-step processes, remembers progress, and resumes exactly after a crash; it descends from Uber's Cadence and is not an AI-agent framework.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工作流每一步进度都持久化，进程/机器崩溃后能从断点精确续跑，不重头也不重复执行
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durable execution persists each workflow step so it resumes exactly after a crash — no restart, no double-run.

optionExplanations: 运行成本翻倍是夸大的说法，真正的代价是复杂度而不是成本直接翻番。
工作流引擎本身并不天然拖慢匹配速度，它管的是状态持久化而不是处理延迟。
引入新框架不是零代价的，团队要学新概念、多维护一个组件，不能毫无顾虑地随便上。
对，代价是团队要学新工具新概念、多一个要运维的组件；但派单是营收关键路径，保证执行和内建容错通常物超所值。
optionExplanations_en: Doubling operating cost is an overstatement — the real cost here is complexity, not a straight doubling of spend.
The workflow engine doesn't inherently slow matching down — what it manages is state persistence, not added processing latency.
Adopting a new framework isn't free — the team has to learn new concepts and maintain one more component, so it shouldn't be adopted without any consideration.
Right, the cost is new concepts to learn and one more component to operate; but for a revenue-critical dispatch path, guaranteed execution and built-in fault tolerance are usually worth it.

scenario: 比较垂直扩容和水平扩容这两种扩展手段在「扩展上限与容错」这一个维度上的差别。
scenario_en: Compare vertical scaling and horizontal scaling on the single dimension of scaling ceiling and fault tolerance.
q: 在扩展上限与容错这个维度上，垂直扩容和水平扩容的区别是？
q_en: On scaling ceiling and fault tolerance, how do vertical and horizontal scaling differ?
options: 垂直扩容的扩展上限一直被普遍认为是无穷大的，而且天然就具备相当强大的容错能力
垂直扩容快但贵、升级要停机、终会到顶、单机一挂全挂；水平扩容加机器就能持续扩展并具备容错
水平扩容存在一个业界公认、无法突破的硬性机器数量上限
在这个流量量级上两种扩容方式被认为完全等价，没有区别
why: 垂直扩容是权宜之计：贵、要停机、有物理上限、单点故障，加冗余也只是创可贴，这个规模的系统里几乎不值得讨论，水平扩容才是正解。
why_en: Vertical scaling is quick but expensive, capped, downtime-prone, and a single point of failure, while horizontal scaling adds servers for capacity and fault tolerance.
tradeoff: 垂直扩容的实现速度 vs 水平扩容的上限与容错
options_en: Vertical scaling has always been widely treated as having a limitless ceiling and as naturally possessing quite strong fault tolerance.
Vertical scaling is fast but expensive, needs downtime, hits a ceiling, and is a single point of failure; horizontal scaling adds servers for ongoing capacity and fault tolerance.
Horizontal scaling is bound by an industry-recognized, unbreakable hard cap on machines.
At this traffic scale the two scaling approaches are treated as fully equivalent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一台机器升级得更强——加 CPU/内存/磁盘。就一台机器，但更猛；升级要关机改配置、且终有物理上限
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical scaling (scale up) makes one machine more powerful (more CPU/RAM/disk); it needs downtime to upgrade and has a hard ceiling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加更多台机器、把负载分摊出去；几乎无上限，还能多副本容错，但需要负载均衡/分片/协调
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling (scale out) adds more machines to share load — near-unlimited and fault-tolerant, but needs load balancing/partitioning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统只有一个该组件，它一挂整个系统就挂；垂直扩容只有一台机器，正是 SPOF
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single point of failure is a component with no backup — if it dies the whole system dies; a single scaled-up box is exactly this.

optionExplanations: 垂直扩容恰恰有物理上限，单机故障还会让整个服务一起挂掉，谈不上容错。
对，垂直扩容快但贵、升级要停机、终会碰到物理上限、单机一挂全挂；水平扩容加机器就能持续扩展，天然具备容错。
水平扩容没有业界公认的机器数硬上限，能扩到多大取决于架构设计而不是某个固定天花板。
在这个千万级司机的规模上两者差异很大，垂直扩容早晚碰壁，水平扩容才撑得住。
optionExplanations_en: Vertical scaling is exactly the one with a physical ceiling, and a single-machine failure takes the whole service down with it — that's the opposite of fault tolerant.

Right, vertical scaling is fast but expensive, needs downtime to upgrade, eventually hits a ceiling, and a single failure takes everything down; horizontal scaling keeps growing by adding machines and is naturally fault tolerant.
There's no industry-recognized hard cap on machine count for horizontal scaling — how far it goes depends on the architecture, not a fixed ceiling.
At tens-of-millions-of-drivers scale the two differ enormously — vertical scaling eventually hits a wall while horizontal keeps holding up.

scenario: 系统要进一步降延迟、提吞吐：用户与司机遍布全球，而绝大多数查询只关心本地范围内的数据。
scenario_en: The system needs lower latency and higher throughput: users and drivers are global, but most queries only care about local data.
q: 在这个「查询天然本地化」的约束下，最合理的扩展策略是？
q_en: Under this naturally local queries constraint, what is the most reasonable scaling strategy?
options: 按地理区域分片配读副本：服务、消息队列、数据库都按地域拆分
把现有的单体服务器直接升级成规格更大更贵的机器
用随机哈希分片把所有数据彻底打散
所有区域继续共用同一个中心数据库
why: 地理分片让数据和计算靠近用户，既扩容又因缩短物理距离而降延迟；读副本进一步提升读吞吐。服务、队列、数据库都能按地域拆。
why_en: Geographic sharding with read replicas scales the services, queues, and databases while cutting latency by moving data closer to users.
whenOtherWins: 数据没有地域局部性时（如全局去重表），哈希/一致性哈希分片更合适；垂直扩容只配当短期应急。
tradeoff: 按地域分片贴合本地化查询 vs 全局哈希分片贴合无地域性数据
options_en: Shard by geographic region with read replicas, splitting services, queues, and databases by geography.
Directly upgrade the existing monolithic server to a bigger, pricier machine.
Randomly hash-shard the data to spread it evenly with no locality.
Keep all regions sharing the same central database.
optionExplanations: 对，服务、队列、数据库都按地域拆分并配读副本，既贴合查询天然本地化的特性又能持续扩容降延迟。
把单体服务器升级得再大，终究有物理上限，也治不了跨地域的物理延迟。
随机哈希打散会把本来同区域的数据分散到各处，查询要跨分片聚合，反而更慢。
所有区域共用一个中心数据库，等于把地域局部性的优势直接放弃了，还要承受跨洲访问延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Right, sharding service, queue, and database by geography with read replicas both fits the naturally local query pattern and keeps scaling while cutting latency.
Scaling a single server ever bigger still hits a physical ceiling, and it does nothing for cross-region physical latency.
Random hash sharding scatters what would otherwise be same-region data everywhere, forcing queries to aggregate across shards — slower, not faster.
Sharing one central database across all regions throws away the locality advantage entirely and forces every query to eat cross-continent latency.

scenario: 地理分片除了单纯扩容，还顺带带来一个延迟方面的好处。
scenario_en: Geographic sharding does more than add capacity; it also brings a latency benefit.
q: 地理分片除了扩展容量，还有什么附带收益？
q_en: Besides capacity scaling, what extra benefit does geographic sharding provide?
options: 省去了系统里全部跨区数据复制需求
让所有查询都直接变成纯内存查询
缩短客户端与服务器的物理距离，直接降低延迟
让负载均衡组件从此变得完全不需要
why: 地理分片 = 按地区把「不同用户的不同数据+服务」放到就近的区域机房。附带收益：用户就近访问、物理距离短 → 往返时延 RTT 直接降。扩容 + 降延迟一举两得。
why_en: Geo-sharding partitions different users' data into nearby regional data centers, so besides adding capacity it lowers latency — clients are physically closer (lower RTT). Unlike a CDN, which replicates identical read-only content everywhere, geo-sharding splits distinct data by region.
options_en: It eliminates every need for cross-region data replication.
It turns every query into a pure in-memory lookup.
It shortens the physical distance between clients and servers, directly cutting latency.
It makes load balancing components entirely unnecessary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分片：按用户地区把数据+服务分到就近的区域机房
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geo-sharding partitions data and services into regional data centers close to their users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络：把同一份静态只读内容缓存到各地边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches the same read-only static content at edge nodes worldwide.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往返时延：请求到达再返回的总时间，主要受物理距离影响
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the round-trip time of a request, dominated by physical distance.

optionExplanations: 地理分片不会消除所有跨区复制需求，某些全局数据仍可能需要跨区同步。
地理分片改变的是数据放在哪个机房，不会把磁盘查询变成纯内存查询。
对，用户就近访问同区域机房，物理距离缩短直接降低往返时延，扩容和降延迟一举两得。
负载均衡在分片后依然需要，只是均衡的范围缩小到区域内，不会被彻底取消。
optionExplanations_en: Geo sharding doesn't eliminate all cross-region replication — some genuinely global data may still need to sync across regions.
Geo sharding changes which data center holds the data; it doesn't turn disk queries into pure in-memory ones.
Right, users hit a nearby regional data center, and the shorter physical distance directly cuts round-trip latency — scaling and lower latency in one move.
Load balancing is still needed after sharding, just scoped within a region — it isn't eliminated altogether.

scenario: 地理分片后，绝大多数就近查询只落在一个分片内即可完成。
scenario_en: After geographic sharding, most nearby-driver queries can be answered inside one shard.
q: 地理分片后，什么时候才需要跨分片的 scatter-gather 查询？
q_en: After geographic sharding, when do you need cross-shard scatter-gather queries?
options: 每次算费用预估时都需要
每次司机上线或下线切换状态时都需要触发一次
系统里的所有写操作都需要
当就近搜索落在分片边界上、搜索半径覆盖多个分片时
why: scatter-gather = 一个查询单片答不完，要「撒(scatter)」到多个分片各算一部分、再「聚(gather)」合并结果——慢(等最慢的分片 + 合并)。地理分片后绝大多数就近查询只落一个分片，省掉了 scatter-gather；只有搜索半径跨分片边界时才需要扇出多片再合并。
why_en: Scatter-gather fans a query out to many shards for partial results and merges them — slow. Geo-sharding keeps most proximity searches inside one shard; you only scatter-gather when a search radius crosses a shard boundary.
options_en: It's needed every time a fare estimate is computed.
It's needed every single time a driver toggles online or offline status.
It's needed for every write operation in the system.
It's needed when a proximity search sits near a shard boundary and its radius spans multiple shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次查询同时发给多个分片、再合并各分片结果的查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather is a query pattern that fans a request out to multiple shards and merges their results.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  Q1["就近查询·市中心"] --> S1["分片A 单片完成 ✓"]
  Q2["查询在分片边界·半径跨片"] --> G["scatter：发给 A+B+C"]
  G --> M["gather：合并结果"]
optionExplanations: 算费用预估通常只涉及本区域的路线数据，不需要跨分片扇出查询。
司机上线切换状态是单个司机的写操作，落在它所在的那一个分片里就够了。
写操作本身不需要跨分片聚合结果，那是查询侧才有的扇出合并逻辑。
对，只有搜索半径覆盖多个分片边界时，才需要向多个分片扇出查询再合并结果。
optionExplanations_en: Fare estimation usually only touches route data within one region, no cross-shard fan-out required.
A driver toggling status is a single-driver write that lands in whichever one shard they belong to.
Writes don't need cross-shard result aggregation — that fan-out-and-merge logic only applies to reads.
Right, only when the search radius spans multiple shard boundaries does the query need to fan out to several shards and merge results.

scenario: 分片系统需要同时解决数据均匀分布和节点增减时的重平衡问题。
scenario_en: A sharded system must solve both even data distribution and rebalancing when nodes are added or removed.
q: 分片系统里怎么处理数据均匀分布和故障重平衡？
q_en: How should a sharded system handle even distribution and failure rebalancing?
options: 用一致性哈希分布数据，配合跨服务器复制策略保证容错与高可用
所有写入都按轮询方式依次轮流写入每一个分片节点
按数据插入的先后顺序取模决定分片
节点增减时全部靠人工手动迁移数据
why: 一致性哈希让节点增减时只迁移少量数据、分布均匀；复制策略保证单分片故障不丢数据、服务不中断。
why_en: Consistent hashing distributes data evenly and eases rebalancing, while replication across servers preserves fault tolerance and availability.
options_en: Use consistent hashing to distribute data, paired with cross-server replication for fault tolerance and availability.
Every write goes round-robin, taking turns landing on each shard node in sequence.
Shard by taking the insertion order modulo the shard count.
Manually migrate data by hand whenever nodes are added or removed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点增减时只需重新映射一小部分数据的哈希分片方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing is a sharding scheme where adding or removing a node only remaps a small fraction of the data.

optionExplanations: 对，一致性哈希让节点增减时只需迁移少量数据并保持均匀分布，复制策略再保证单分片故障不丢数据。
按轮询写入并不保证数据分布均匀，也没有解决节点变化时怎么重新分配数据的问题。
按插入顺序取模在节点数变化时会导致几乎所有数据的映射都要重算，迁移量极大。
完全靠人工迁移在这个规模下既慢又容易出错，不具备可持续的扩展性。
optionExplanations_en: Right, consistent hashing keeps distribution even and only moves a small slice of data when nodes join or leave, while replication keeps a single shard's failure from losing data or interrupting service.
Round-robin writes don't guarantee even distribution and don't address how to reassign data when nodes change.
Modulo by insertion order forces nearly every key's mapping to be recomputed whenever the node count changes, causing massive migration.
Relying entirely on manual migration is slow and error-prone at this scale — it isn't a sustainable way to scale.

scenario: 面试官按候选人级别设定不同的通过标准，这是 Uber 这道题对中级（E4）候选人的达标线。
scenario_en: Interviewers set different bars by candidate level; this is the Uber problem's bar for an intermediate E4 candidate.
q: Uber 题对中级（E4）候选人的达标线是什么？
q_en: What is the passing bar for an intermediate E4 candidate on the Uber problem?
options: 必须在现场深入讲透 3 个以上的深挖话题才行，浅尝辄止的讲法完全不算合格
清晰定义 API 与数据模型，给出满足需求的高层设计，意识到位置查询需要空间索引（不必定方案），至少给出锁问题的 good 方案
要求候选人必须现场完完全全从零手写出一份完整、可以真实编译并成功稳定运行起来的 quad-tree 空间索引实现代码
要求候选人准确背出 DynamoDB 官网定价页面上写着的具体数字
why: E4 重广度（约 80/20）：功能完备的高层设计加知道位置查询需要某种空间索引加至少 DB 状态锁级别的方案即可达标。
why_en: A mid-level candidate needs clear APIs and data model, a working high-level design, awareness that a spatial index is needed, and at least the good locking solution.
options_en: Must thoroughly deep-dive on three or more topics live on the spot; a shallow treatment doesn't count as passing at all.
Clearly define the API and data model, produce a working high-level design, recognize that location queries need a spatial index, and give at least the good locking solution.
Requires the candidate to hand-write, completely from scratch on the spot, a complete quad-tree spatial index implementation that genuinely compiles and runs successfully and stably.
The candidate must accurately recite the exact numbers printed on DynamoDB's official pricing page.
optionExplanations: E4 更看重广度而不是现场深挖三个以上话题，深挖数量不是这一级别的达标线。
对，清晰的 API 与数据模型、功能完备的高层设计、知道位置查询要用空间索引、至少给出锁的 good 方案，这些凑齐就够 E4 达标。
现场手写完整可跑的 quad-tree 实现超出了这一级别的期望，意识到需要空间索引就够。
背出具体定价数字不是考察点，E4 需要的是设计判断力而不是记忆力。
optionExplanations_en: E4 is weighted toward breadth, not live-deep-diving three or more topics — depth count isn't the bar at this level.
Right, a clear API and data model, a functionally complete high-level design, awareness that location queries need some spatial index, and at least a good lock solution together clear the E4 bar.
Hand-writing a complete, runnable quad-tree implementation live is beyond this level's expectations — just recognizing the need for a spatial index is enough.
Reciting exact pricing numbers isn't what's being assessed — E4 needs design judgment, not memorization.

scenario: 这是 Uber 这道题对高级（E5）候选人的达标线。
scenario_en: This is the Uber problem's bar for a senior E5 candidate.
q: 高级（E5）候选人的达标线是什么？
q_en: What is the passing bar for a senior E5 candidate?
options: 只要能大致画完一版高层设计草图，细节全部略过也算合格
要求候选人必须一字不差地背出所有 Redis 命令的完整参数列表和具体使用方法才算合格
快速过完高层设计，深入讨论至少 2 个深挖，并能讲清各架构选择对扩展性、性能、可维护性的利弊
要求候选人当场独立发明出一套全新的匹配排序算法
why: E5 约 60/40 广深比：高层设计要快，把时间花在至少 2 个深挖的细节与权衡上；面试官适度提示是可以接受的。
why_en: A senior candidate should speed through the high-level design and discuss at least two deep dives in detail with clear architectural trade-offs.
options_en: Just roughly sketching a version of the high-level design and skipping every detail counts as passing.
Requires the candidate to recite, word for word without a single mistake, the full parameter list and exact usage method of every Redis command to pass.
Speed through the high-level design and dive deep into at least two topics with clear trade-offs on scalability, performance, and maintainability.
The candidate must independently invent an entirely new matching-ranking algorithm on the spot.
optionExplanations: 只画个大致草图、细节全略过达不到 E5 要求的深度，广度够但深度不够。
背出所有 Redis 命令参数不是重点，E5 考的是能不能把架构选择的利弊讲清楚。
对，高层设计要快速过完，把时间留给至少 2 个深挖话题，讲清各选择对扩展性、性能、可维护性的取舍。
现场独立发明全新排序算法超出预期，E5 允许基于已知方案做合理取舍，不要求从零创新。
optionExplanations_en: A rough sketch with all details skipped falls short of E5's depth bar — breadth alone isn't enough.
Reciting every Redis command's parameters isn't the point — E5 tests whether you can articulate the tradeoffs behind architecture choices.
Right, race through the high-level design and spend the saved time on at least two deep dives that spell out the tradeoffs on scalability, performance, and maintainability.
Independently inventing a brand-new ranking algorithm on the spot is beyond expectations — E5 allows reasoned tradeoffs on known approaches, not from-scratch invention.

scenario: 这是 Uber 这道题对 Staff+ 候选人的显著标志。
scenario_en: This is the Uber problem's clear signal for a Staff+ candidate.
q: Staff+ 候选人的显著标志是什么？
q_en: What is the clear signal of a Staff+ candidate?
options: 约 40/60 广深比：主动深入 3 个以上关键领域，用实战经验支撑方案，最好让面试官也学到新东西
把全部 45 分钟的宝贵时间都完完整整地花在画一张极其精细复杂的整体组件架构图上面去了，别的都不做
全程被动地等待面试官指路，自己完全不主动向前推进任何设计工作
把文章里介绍的全部方案逐字逐句一字不差地原样背诵出来
why: Staff+ 期待极高的主动性与深度：自己发现问题、给出经过实战检验的方案；面试官只聚焦不引路，聊完还有所收获是最好的信号。
why_en: A staff-plus candidate proactively dives deep into three or more areas with practical insight, ideally teaching the interviewer something new.
options_en: Roughly a forty-sixty breadth-to-depth ratio: proactively going deep on three or more areas with practical experience, ideally teaching the interviewer something new.
Spend the entire precious forty-five minutes completely drawing just one extremely detailed, intricate overall component architecture diagram, and nothing else.
Passively wait to be guided by the interviewer the whole time, never proactively pushing the design forward at all.
Recite every solution described in the article word for word, verbatim.
optionExplanations: 对，约 40/60 广深比，主动深入 3 个以上关键领域并用实战经验支撑方案，最好还能让面试官学到新东西。
把 45 分钟全花在一张极其精细的架构图上等于牺牲了深挖的时间，广度都保不住。
全程被动等指路恰恰是 Staff+ 最忌讳的信号，这个级别期待候选人自己发现问题。
逐字背诵文章方案说明没有自己的判断和取舍，体现不出实战经验支撑的深度。
optionExplanations_en: Right, roughly a 40/60 breadth-to-depth ratio, proactively going deep on three or more key areas with battle-tested reasoning — ideally teaching the interviewer something new.
Spending all 45 minutes on one hyper-detailed diagram sacrifices depth time and even breadth suffers.
Passively waiting to be guided the whole time is exactly the red flag Staff+ interviewers watch for — this level expects candidates to surface problems themselves.
Reciting an article's solution verbatim shows no independent judgment or tradeoff reasoning, missing the depth that real experience provides.
